utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Good morning. Mr. Niemann, would you like to call your next IN witness, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. Before I do that I would like to correct something I mentioned yesterday. I think I said that the first identification witness would be the ninth. I was mistaken when I said that. It is, in fact, the seventh witness from Mr. Mujcic, but in any event we can change the order around if that is necessary to extend it further down.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Do you intend on submitting a response to the submission of Mr. Wladimiroff?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, we will do, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. When do you plan on submitting that? What is the day, Wednesday. I do not know how your witnesses are going. I have not added up the hours, but just a quick check, I do not think we would get to that witness until July now since we are recessing or adjourning Wednesday of next week.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. It may be that we do not get to the witness. Alternatively, if we get to it, it will be next week. We would expect to submit our response by Tuesday, at least, so the witness could then follow after that time, but it could well be July.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. No later than next Wednesday then, submit your response. If based on the movement of the witnesses that it appears we are going to have to hear from a witness, say, on Wednesday, then you will have to give it to us a little bit sooner so that we can resolve it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: We will do that.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. Very good. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I call Salko Karabasic. MR. SALKO KARABASIC called.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That should be No. 22. Do you - have you a change in the order of your witnesses? I see, the new was 22, the original was 26. I see. You have renumbered them under the new column. OK, very good. Mr. Kay, does that look all right to you? You are both looking a little surprised.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We were expecting someone else.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: But you see in the new column it would be No. 22, in the left-hand column it follows. This is correct. It is the 22nd witness according to the new listing which you submitted June 11th?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Karabasic, would you please take that oath?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your full name is Salko Karabasic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What is your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: March 10th.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where were you born?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Brdjani.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can you just tell us approximately how far Brdjani is from the centre of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One kilometre.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where did you attend your primary school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your secondary education?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I only have four grades of the elementary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: If it is a matter of concern, the date of birth does not give the year, only the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I am sorry, your Honour. (To the witness): Can you tell me the year that you were born in?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Up until 1992 at the commencement of the war in Kozarac, where had you lived during your life?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Kozarac, in Brdjani.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What was your occupation during that period, up until 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was a labourer.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where did you work?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Kozarac, at the sawmill.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you do your military service?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When did you do your military service?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where did you do your military service?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Celje in Slovenia.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Are you by religion Muslim?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were you involved in the Territorial Defence or in the JNA immediately prior to the commencement of the war in Kozarac in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were you on reserve service in the Territorial Defence at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Is that in common with most other people who do military service in the former Yugoslavia prior to that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know the accused in these proceedings, Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: For how long have you known him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have known him since I was -- since he was 15 years old.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where did you come to know him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would pass by his house every day when I was going to work or coming back from work.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The place where you worked was at the Trnopolje end of Kozarac, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not have to cross the road to Banja Luka; it was right next to the road to Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: That is right. You lived up in Brdjani which was up towards the mountain?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: During the time that you lived in Kozarac up until 1992, did you see the accused Dule Tadic only rarely or occasionally or did you see him often?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Occasionally.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Are you able to describe where he lived in the town of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can you tell us where that was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He lived by the school, above the new school, the new large school, and basically across from the school above the Restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was there a restaurant attached to his premises, was there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you say "above the restaurant", what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In that direction towards, up to Kozarac from the Banja Luka road there was a Restaurant and then there was a house belonging to Banda, and then above his house up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I see. So that was a rather large building which was known locally as the "Restaurant", that is what you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The place that you describe where Dule Tadic lived, so far as you are aware, did he live there all the time that he was in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I remember, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know what he did, what his occupation was, before the war in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you know his wife?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What was her name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Vidovic, Mira. Mira Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you know any people who were friends or seemed to be associates of the accused Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did know some of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Are you able to name any of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Emir Karabasic was a very good friend of his.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: You mentioned his wife's family, Vidovic. Do you know where they lived, where his wife's family lived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Vidovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know what her father's name was, his wife's father's name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mira.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I am sorry, do you know what the accused Dule Tadic's wife's father's name, first name was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I know Radovan.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you knew the accused Dule Tadic in the town of Kozarac, did you know him to be a man who was clean shaven or did he have a beard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sometimes he would have a very short beard, that day when I saw him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know whether he was engaged in any sporting activities in and about the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I heard from others that he was into karate, that he was training karate.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Apart from when you saw him in the town at Kozarac, did you see him in other places in and about the area or the region of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I saw him, I saw him that day and then I did not see him afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, I am asking you prior to 1992. You said earlier in your evidence that you had seen him at his house when you used to go to work in Kozarac. I am asking you other than at that place did you see him in other places about the region of Kozarac prior to 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you see the accused, Dule Tadic, prior to 1992 in another place or other places in the area of Kozarac, but not necessarily in the town of Kozarac, on an occasion or occasionally prior to 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see him because up until 1992 I was always in Kozarac. I was not leaving Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I think you said earlier that you knew where his wife's father lived.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Just tell us again, where was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Where his father lived?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Do you mean Dule's father?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, no. You said a moment ago that you knew where his wife's father lived. Do you know where that is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I knew he lived in Vidovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Is that near to where you used to live?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is about half a kilometre from my village to Vidovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you from time to time see people in and about the area of Vidovici? This is prior to 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you ever see the accused's wife, Mira Vidovic, in that area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you ever see the accused in that area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can you recall when the attack on Kozarac began?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 24th May.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Approximately what time in the day did it commence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It commenced somewhere in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was that early afternoon or late afternoon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Early.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where were you at the time at the commencement of the attack on Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was in the mountaineers' lodge.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where is that in relation to the town of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is from Kozarac, first you get to Brdjani, then to Vidovici and then this is about 500 or 600 metres from Vidovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What were you doing at this place when the attack commenced?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were there on guard.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: On guard as what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were there as part of the reserve units.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Of the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know who was the Commander of the Territorial Defence at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Vaskan Kulasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you were there on guard how were you dressed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were dressed in JNA uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where did you get that JNA uniform from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I got it from the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How long before 1992 did you collect that uniform from the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Exactly eight months before the war. I cannot remember the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were you armed at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, when I got the uniform I got the weapon as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: On the day of the attack on 24th May 1992, were you armed on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: With what were you armed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A rifle, model M48.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Is this a World War II type weapon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is an old weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you have any ammunition?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 25 pieces.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can you tell me just exactly what it is that you were doing there at this particular time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was there, my shift was on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What were you doing? What were you guarding?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were guarding, first, we were in front of the Local Commune in Kozarac and we were guarding that and then by the store so that people would not loot the store, and then after that they transferred us to the mountaineer lodge up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you say "they" who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Approximately how many members of the Territorial Defence were with you up at this mountain lodge above Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know exactly the number because we were constantly changing shifts.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: During the course of the bombardment or attack on Kozarac, did you yourself personally encounter any attacking Serb forces and did you or did you not fire your weapon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not fire a single bullet when I was at the mountain lodge.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: For how long did you stay up in the mountain lodge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Until it started, they started shelling and at that time everybody went in their own directions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you at this stage abandon your rifle and uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes ---

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What did you do -----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- the same day.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What did you do with your rifle and uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I took it home. I buried the rifle and the bullets and I know where they are and I took my uniform and left it at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you then join your family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was looking for my family for one day and then I found them, and then I joined them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can you recall what day this was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean when I found my family?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: That is right, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was Monday, 25th.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: 25th May 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you found your family what did you do then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then we were hiding in refuges and basements and we were looking for the safest and largest basements, and this is how we were hiding.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you go back to your house on 26th May 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only occasionally to see my house and then I would go back to those basements.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you went back to see your house, did you see the approaching Serb forces coming towards your village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We saw in Kozarac, they were already in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I see. So what did you do then? What did you do next?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What did I do? I went back. I found my family and I stayed with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where did you stay with your family when you went back?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were in a house, one woman's house, her name was Suada Blazevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: In what town or village was this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is right between Brdjani and Vidovici, halfway between those two places.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We stayed there, I am not sure, that whole day, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Then did you go to the town of Vidovici itself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Eno Mehmedagic from Brdjani came and he remained at home when the army came in, and when the tank went into Brdjani they forced him out and he came up to Vidovici and he told us, "Get lost from here and walk towards Kozarac; if you do not do that, then they will shoot all of you".

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What day was this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was on 27th.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you do that? Did you head towards Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we were by -- we were staying with Radovan and Ostoja Vidovic, and they told us, "You had better leave otherwise we will have to go, we will get in trouble with you as well". This is what we did and we left; all of us who were there in that village, we left.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: So you were seeking refuge, were you, with Radovan Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, with Radovan and Ostoja Vidovic. They allowed us to come in.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Is the Radovan Vidovic that you were staying with, or who was giving you shelter, the father-in-law of the accused Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: So you then left, did you, on 27th the village of Vidovici and travelled towards Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was quarter to 12 when Eno came and brought us the news and then we left that village and headed towards Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you say "we", was it just you or was there a number of people walking in that direction or travelling in that direction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A number of people that were staying up there in Vidovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Are you able to give an approximate or an estimate of the number of people who started to move in this convoy towards Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not give you an exact number, but there must have been at least 200 or 300 people there, women, children.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What was the nationality of the majority of the people in that column?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How were the people travelling? Were they all travelling on foot or were some on motorized vehicles or horse driven vehicles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were tractors, a few tractors. Most of the people were on foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I would ask you to look, if you would, please, at Exhibit D12, which is a map of the region. Could you just examine that map for a moment and just orientate yourself, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What I want you to do for me, please, if you would, is we will put this particular map, D12, on the overhead projector which is beside you there, not in front of you but beside you -- I will ask Miss Sutherland to help you -- then I will ask you with a finger or with a pointer, if you would, to give us the general direction that the column marched on its way from Vidovici down towards Kozarac. So if we can put that on the overhead projector? You are going to have to point to this on the overhead projector because even though it will come up on your television screen, if you point to it on the screen we do not see what you are pointing at. So you have to point to it as you see it there. So can you generally trace the course that you followed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Vidovici towards the Mutnik Mosque, and then down Kozarac towards the Banja Luka road, and somewhere here the road bifurcates and one branch goes to Kalate.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can that map be returned to the Registrar? As this column, march of people came down towards Kozarac, did you see any Serb forces or their equipment in and about the area -----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We saw Serb forces as soon as we reached Brdjani and they were all lined up along the streets.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did they appear to you to be regular JNA or were they irregular forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: JNA members.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you see whether they had any military or heavy military equipment there at the time with them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a tank in Brdjani.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you see whether any of the houses or buildings had been set on fire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, some were already.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you see whether there were any bodies of people that had been killed in and about the area as you moved down?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean in Brdjani?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you subsequently see people that had been killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Brdjani, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, later on after you left Brdjani?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we entered Kozarac then, yes, I did see.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: As you came down, in towards Kozarac, did more people join this column?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were members of your family in the column with you as you were moving down?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were they your immediate family, that is, your wife and children?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: They were with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What about your brothers or sisters or mother and father, were they also in the column?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were also in the column, but were not together. We were not in one group as we moved with the column.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: As the column march came down into Kozarac, what happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we came down the Brdjani road to Mutnik Mosque, then we followed -- first, there is the old school, that is where the TO had its premises, then beyond the school is a well, there you turn to Kalate, and on the corner itself there was a kiosk, chickens and bread were sold there. There was a kiosk there. A stand was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I would ask you to look at this photograph that you are now shown. Might this be marked for identification 224? Could that be marked for identification 224? Could you just examine this photograph for me, please, and tell me if you can recognise ---

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: -- what it is a photograph of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What is it a photograph of? I am sorry, what is it a photograph of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This picture here shows the Local Commune and further up is a sort of a club or a sort of a pub, or something like that, and here by this poplar was this kiosk. Now it has gone, you see.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I tender the photograph, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Prosecutors's Exhibit 224 will be admitted. MR. NIEMANN (To the witness): Mr. Karabasic, would you please now have that photograph -- we will put it on the screen -- and with the pointer again I will ask you to point, if you would, please, to various points on this photograph. Perhaps that could be expanded to its full size? Firstly, just looking at the photograph there, could you put the pointer in the direction of the road towards Kalate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here to the right is the road to Kalate.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: You will need to do it on the projector, otherwise we cannot see what you are pointing to if you point to the television screen. You will need to point to the photograph itself.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Over to your right, Mr. Karabasic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here, this is Kalate road to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: OK then. Can you tell me the direction of Marsala Tita Street, the main street in Kozarac, which direction is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, here behind this building, behind this tall building, but you cannot see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can you point to the place where that kiosk was that you referred to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The kiosk was here right next to this poplar tree. It was on the very corner and the kiosk was right behind it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Perhaps that photograph can be returned to the Registrar? Your Honours, we are having additional copies made which we will make available. As you came down to that place you just pointed to on the photograph, can you tell me what happened, what you saw?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We passed by this old school and then this well here and immediately to the right, you turn to Kalate, that is where Dule Tadic was standing, right across it by the kiosk on the other side but on the side of the road was Goran Borovnica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What else did you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I came up there was singled out there, my brother, Ismet Karabasic, and Foric. They were next to this koka.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you remember Foric's first name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Redzep.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you say "next to the koka", are you referring to the kiosk?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I mean the kiosk. It was all in one.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then Dule Tadic pointed with his finger and said to Borovnica, "Take this out", and then he got him by the top of the neck and brought him as a third one next to the kiosk; and my son who was going next to me in the column, he turned back to see my brother, Ekrem, and Dule told to Borovnica, "And get this one too", and he came and grabbed my son, and I was pulling him and he was pulling him, and we were both pushing him and pulling him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I just need to go over that a little bit more slowly. The first one that you saw taken out of the line was your brother, Ekrem, by Borovnica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Then you say that your son who was with you, was he -- was your son with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What was your son's name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sejdo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Borovnica then came down, did he, towards where Sejdo was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He came down, yes, and I tried to pull my son towards me, and he was pulling him from me and he snatched him away from me and he said: "Do you want to come here too?" he told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where was your son Sejdo then taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Together with Ekrem and Enver and Redzo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you say "together with" them, do you mean over towards the kiosk?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where was Dule Tadic, as best you can -----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was standing in the same place where I had seen him first. I would not -- I would recognise the square metre where he was standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: For how long were you able to see Dule Tadic as you approached this place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was brief, like going across this room here, I should say that was ---

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How close?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- that was it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I am sorry. How close was the closest that you got to Dule Tadic as you went past this place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not more than two and a half to three metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were the weather conditions clear or was there anything about the weather that made it difficult to see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a very nice day.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was your view in any way obstructed by anything as this happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you hear Dule Tadic's voice?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you recognise that voice?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The person that Tadic was with, Borovnica, had you seen him before in the town of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you know him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you observe how Dule Tadic was dressed on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I saw it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How was he dressed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was in some multi-coloured uniform and he had a multi-coloured hat on his head.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was he armed at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How was he armed, with what was he armed, I should say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had a pistol in his belt and had some automatic weapon in his hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was it Dule Tadic that was giving instructions or was Borovnica just acting on his own accord?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dule Tadic was issuing orders and Borovnica was executing them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: After your son and your two brothers were taken over to this kiosk that you described, what happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He took out another one, Meho Mujkan, the fifth one.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What occurred then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And Dule ordered again, and Borovnica again approached us and took out Meho Mujkan and he joined the other four.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: At this stage when this was happening was the column still moving along?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they said, "Slower, slower, slower, slower, short step, short step".

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: But, nevertheless, it was still continuing to move, was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: In what direction was the column continuing to move?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Towards Banja Luka/Prijedor road.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you at one stage get close in the column to where that kiosk was, where the men were standing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I passed by my brother, Ismet. He was not more than two metres away from me. On the corner by the kiosk was my brother, Ismet, and all he managed to do was show me, indicate with his hand, to move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did Ismet give you a sign to keep moving on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, with his hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How was Ismet standing against that kiosk that you can remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, he was standing like this and had his hands as so against the kiosk, and he slightly turned his head towards the road and only made a slight sign to show that we should move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did the column move on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Would you look, please, at this plan that I now show you? Might that be marked for identification as 225? That is not a plan that you yourself drew, but by looking at the markings on it and the shape of the plan itself, are you able to recognise what it is a plan of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the plan next to this koka on this small junction. To the right is where the road branches off to Kalate, and if you continue a little bit down here you come to the tower.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: OK. I would like you with the pen that I now give you, and putting the thing on the plan, would you please draw for me with the pen on the overhead projector, firstly, the direction that the column was marching? You might do that with an arrow, if you would please, and put a "C" above the arrow. So if you could just draw for me an arrow in the direction the column was marching?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness marked on the plan) This is where it goes to Kalate and here to the tower.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: OK. The tower is Kula, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The first mark, would you put an arrow showing the direction the column was going? Just make it an arrow.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness marked on the plan).

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Right. I want you to look at the top of the plan, if you would, for me and do you see the words there "Mutnik Mosque"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry, I do apologise. I put it upside-down.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: That is OK.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I turned the map upside-down.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: It is easier for you to look at it this way. Perhaps you might draw an arrow in the direction that you remember the column was marching.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness marked on the plan). This is where the column moved.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Would you put a "C" under that little arrow that you have just drawn? Thank you. As best you can remember, would you put a "W" at the spot where you say that well was in front of the old school which was used for the TO building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is where it was. (The witness marked on the plan).

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Could you put a "T", the letter "T", where you say you saw Dule Tadic, approximately the spot where you saw Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness marked on the plan).

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Could you put the letter "B" in the spot where you say you saw Borovnica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness marked on the plan).

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Would you put the letter "K" in the spot where you say that kiosk is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness marked on the plan).

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Would you mark with an "X" the spot where you say those men were lined up against that kiosk?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness marked on the plan).

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Would you draw the wall of the kiosk against which they were standing, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness marked on the plan).

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you. I tender that, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour, but we would like to have a copy of it because we had no clean one to draw for ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I can supply one.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will have a copy made for you. You want a copy of the one that is marked?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will have that at the recess, if not sooner. I think it can be done now if you are not going to continue to use it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, I am not, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 225 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: You said a moment ago in your evidence, Mr. Karabasic, that the column was moving, although it was moving slowly it was continuing to move down the street, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you then go on down towards the bottom of Marsala Tita Street ---

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: -- in the column? Did you hear anything as you walked down the street, down Marsala Tita Street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where did you go after you got to the bottom of Marsala Tita Street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then we headed right towards Kozarusa.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What about your son Sejdo did you ever see him again from that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Never again. I never saw him again.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your brother, Ekrem, have you ever seen him again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How old was your brother, Ekrem?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was born in 54.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What did he do for a living?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was a worker.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was he involved in the army or the JNA at the time of the attack on Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was in the Territorial Defence with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When he was pulled out of the line on that day that you have described on 27th, was he armed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That day, you mean, or before that?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, just at that moment he was pulled out of the line by Borovnica -- that time when he was in the line there, was he armed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would not know. I do not know who pulled him out because he was in the beginning of the column so I do not remember. I do not know who it was that pulled him out and whether he had anything because when I came up he was already singled out, standing there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I am sorry, yes. My question was not clear. When you saw him there, did he appear to be armed at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: How could he be when he was bare handed brought there?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was he dressed in ordinary civilian clothes or was in military uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Civilian.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What about your brother, Ismet, when was he born?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you saw him there at that place on the corner near the kiosk on 27th May 1992, did you notice whether or not he was armed in any way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was he dressed in civilian clothes or in military clothes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Civilian.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: From that day until now have you ever seen your brother, Ismet, again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When was your son Sejdo born?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: At the time that he was taken out of the line on 27th May 1992, at that place in Kozarac, was he armed, so far as you could see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He did not have anything. He was no member of any organisation. He was never in anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was he dressed in civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Civilian.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What of Redzo Foric? Was Redzo Foric in civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know approximately how old he would be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He, I think, is like Ismet, around 1950.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was he dressed in civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: From that day till this, have you ever seen him again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What happened to the column after you went down towards the end of the main street in Kozarac, where did you go then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We turned right towards Prijedor, towards Kozarusa.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where did you go? Did you go to Kozarusa?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What happened when you got to Kozarusa?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There the Serb army command was, that is where we were separated, that is women, old and children to one side and men to the other. That is where the separation took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: On this walk towards Kozarusa did you see any dead bodies of people beside the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I did see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did they appear to you to be dressed in civilian clothes or military clothes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Civilian.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did any of them appear to have in their possession arms, military weapons of any sort?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those who were killed, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you got to Kozarusa you say that people were being separated out. Were you separated from your family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was separated.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was taken on a bus to Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: With you on that bus were there women and children or was it only males that you could see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Where I was on the bus there were only men.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was the nationality of these men Muslim, as you could see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How long did it take you to get to Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It took us approximately from Kozarac maybe an hour-and-a-half to two hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What happened when you got to Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we came to Keraterm they took us out of the bus. They unloaded us and then the bus went somewhere else and then new buses would arrive with new people.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you enter into any of the buildings there at the camp or did you just stand there once you had been taken off the buses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How long did you stay in this place where you were taken off the buses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not tell you exactly, but maybe four to five hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then the buses, new buses, were arriving and they were loading people on the buses and taking them to Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What happened to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was put on a bus and I went to Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did anything happen in the buses on the way from Keraterm to Omarska that you could see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was night already and in my bus where I was nothing happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What time did you arrive at Omarska approximately? Can you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was maybe 4 o'clock in the morning, the dawn was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was this the next day, was it, 28th May 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was a Thursday, 28th.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you arrived at Omarska what happened then to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They parked the bus there by the door, and we came out. We had our hands behind our neck, by our arms, and then the buses were taken away.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were taken up there to another floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you say "up there to another floor", were you taken to the large garage type building where the mining equipment, trucks, were kept and repaired?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we passed by the garage and then we went up, we turned right and went up to another floor. There was a room there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: So it was an upstairs section of this large garage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: On your first night when you were in Omarska camp, did you ask to go to the toilet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What happened when you did that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I asked to go to the toilet and they allowed me. The guard there who was in the hall allowed me to go there and I went into the toilet and there was no handle on the door. There was no handle. So I went into the bathroom and he cursed my mother and he said, "Close the door behind you", and I tried to close the door but the door immediately locked and then he cursed my mother again, my Muslim mother, and he said, "You will see now" and then he went into the hall, and then he found another handle and came back and opened the door and then made me force, made me face the wall and then we was beating me with the rifle on my back and on my head.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What part of the rifle did he beat you with on your back and on your head?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With the butt of the rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was he hitting you with the rifle at full force?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you lose several teeth as a result of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: About eight days later were you then taken for interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Something like that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What were they endeavouring to find out during the course of your interrogation, do you recall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were trying to find out whether there was some extremists there, whether I was among the extremists, and that is what they wanted to know. That was the interrogation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How long did you stay in this garage building, the large garage building, how long were you kept there for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: During the whole time while I was at Omarska camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: While you were at Omarska camp did you ever see any dead bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you see these bodies on regular occasions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, regularly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were these dead bodies dressed in civilian or military clothes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Civilian.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: From what you were able to see, did these people seem to be inmates, prisoners, in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where did you see these bodies on a regular occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When they took us to lunch or breakfast, here across pista, by the house there, we would see the bodies around the white house lying on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How many approximately did you often see? How many bodies would you often see in this place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not tell you exactly, but we were not allowed to raise our heads and look up. We would just, sort of, look to the ground and then try to see something and I could not even count those bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What was the food like when you were in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Bad, really bad.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you hear people being beaten during the time that you were in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, when we went to the lunch people were taken out frequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: During the course of the night were people beaten while you were in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was impossible. It was impossible how they beat them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you see people that came back with wounds and injuries as a result of what had happened to them, the beatings that they had received?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I saw people who came back and then we would try to put compresses on them, we would take our shirts and t-shirts off and put them in the cold water and then put it as a compress on the people that were beaten.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was the period of time leading up to Petrov Dan a particularly bad time for beatings in the Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a bad period.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: For the benefit of the court, can you tell us what your understanding of Petrov Dan is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not sure. It is a Serbian holiday, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When does this Serbian holiday fall, approximately?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not sure of exact date. I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Is it in the month of July?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Apart from your involvement in the Territorial Defence and when you did your military service, were you in any other way involved in any military or paramilitary groups which were offering or providing armed resistance to the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: To your knowledge, was there anyone who lived in the Kozarac area who looked in any way or very much like the accused, Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there was nobody that looked like him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you ever hear of any instance where the accused Dule Tadic was mistaken by somebody else who lived in the area on the basis that this person looked like him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I have not heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I would ask you, if you would please, to look around the courtroom and tell me if you see the person that you know and recognise as Dule Tadic in the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there he is. He is sitting over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Is he the gentleman -- can you just tell me where precisely he is sitting; just point to him and describe him for me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He is sitting there between those two policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Might the record mention that, your Honour?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes. The record will reflect that the witness identified the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: In June 1995 were you interviewed by an investigator from the Office of the Prosecutor of the International Tribunal at your home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was there taken at that stage a written statement in the English language of the interview that was conducted with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was that statement that was taken in the English language produced into writing and read to you in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you then proceed to sign your name on that statement that was read to you in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Since coming to The Hague to give evidence in these proceedings, has the statement in parts at least been read back to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The part of the statement, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes. Have you noticed that there is at least on one occasion an error in the statement that was taken from you back in June 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Does that error relate to who was taken out of the line and whom you observed being taken out of the line when you were at that place in Kozarac on 27th May 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is exactly that error.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes. Can you just, in your own words, describe to us the error that you observed or noticed when the statement was read to you, as best you can?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was read to me that Ekrem was singled out with Ismet. It was not him. It was Redzo that was singled out with Ismet. That was the mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you saw Dule Tadic at that place in Kozarac on 27th May 1992 when your son Sejdo was taken out of the line, are you sure that it was Dule Tadic that you observed on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A thousand per cent sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I have no further questions, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, cross-examination? We will stand in recess now for 20 minutes, Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, would you like to conduct the cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Mr. Karabasic, I would like to ask you some questions, first of all, about the time when you had left Kozarac town because of the attack upon it and you were in the Vidovici area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not even in Kozarac when the attack commenced on the city.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that. I just want to ask you questions about the time that you had moved from Brdjani to Vidovici and were there sheltering because of the attack on the area.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went to Vidovici somewhere in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In that place shelter was given to you and others from Kozarac by the Vidovic family, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we were staying with Radovan and Ostoja Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In that particular hamlet there are about 10 or 11 houses, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There are nine houses, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were there a large number of people with you taking shelter -----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not give you the exact number but, yes, there were a lot of men, women and children.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But the time came when it was too dangerous for those people to continue giving you shelter and you had to leave Vidovici, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you remember what time you left Vidovici in the convoy on 27th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Quarter to 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The time that you reached Mutnik Mosque in Kozarac, can you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was maybe 12.30 or sometime around that, 1.00, 1.00, but not more than 1 o'clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Then you moved down Marsala Tita Street, moving ---

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: -- through Kozarac, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we look at the plan you have drawn, Exhibit 224 -- perhaps a copy could be put back in front of the witness?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I think it is 225.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. (To the witness): You have drawn on that plan by a wavy line the position of the chicken kiosk, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we look at that line, it shows that the kiosk appears to be at an angle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was at an angle.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So that one end of the kiosk faced on to Marsala Tita Street, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And the other end of the kiosk faced on to the road that takes you to Kalate, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we look at the photograph, Exhibit 224 -- the court does not have a copy of this but perhaps it can be put on the monitor -- there is a tree which is right on the junction of Marsala Tita Street and the road that takes us to Kalate, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So looking at that photograph would we be looking at the front of the kiosk, if it was still there, where you would go up to buy chickens?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Do you mean we are looking from the side?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps I could put the question in a different way: did the front of the kiosk face towards the corner of the street, as you have shown it in your plan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The front of the kiosk faced the main street and the window where we were buying newspapers and chicken and bread, and the other side where Borovnica and where Dule were standing, that was the other side of the kiosk and that was behind the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did that part of the kiosk have any windows or offer any service from there, or was it just the end of the kiosk, a blank wall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It did not have any windows. That side had no windows and then the windows where we were buying things were facing the main street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. What time was it about that you got to this place in Marsala Tita Street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It must have been between 12.00 and 1 o'clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: At this stage you were in a column with a group of your family, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, my family, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you remember whether you were at the head of this column that had moved from Vidovici, in the middle or at the end?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was behind the middle of the column.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: About how wide was the column of people? Did it take up the width of the road down Marsala Tita Street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not the whole street, but a larger part of the street, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The scene in Kozarac at this time, was it one where buildings were on fire and there had been damage and destruction to buildings in the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not that much destruction, but some houses were burning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you said that the military were there, did you mean by that the regular JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were they dressed in JNA uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were there many soldiers in this part of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were many soldiers, not that many, but there were soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now about what you say you saw in Kozarac at this time at the junction of Marsala Tita Street with the road to Kalate. You were in a group of your family and did you see Ismet Karabasic singled out from the convoy of people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you see Foric Redzep singled out from the column of people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you see them standing near the kiosk?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I saw that as I approached.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So at some stage before you got there Ismet and Foric had been taken out of the convoy?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not Ismet Foric, Redzep Foric.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I understand, I said Ismet and Foric.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Substituted the name and the last name, Ismet Karabasic, not Ismet Foric.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I think something got missed in the translation. Did you see Ekrem being singled out from the convoy of people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was not singled, he was singled in front of my eyes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your evidence earlier this morning was that it was Dusko Tadic that pointed his finger and said to Goran Borovnica to take Ekrem away from the other people, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Also your son Sejdo was also taken out of the group of people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Sejdo turned his head to see how, how they are removing Ado and then Dule Tadic said, pointed to Sejdo and said, "Take this one out as well".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you said that Sejdo turned his head to see how they were removing, you mentioned a particular name, Ado, who do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sejdo? Ado, Sejdo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You said that Sejdo was taken out of the group of people when he turned his head. Was Sejdo looking at anything in particular at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was looking after my brother, Ekrem. He was looking at Goran taking Ekrem out, Goran Borovnica taking Ekrem out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So was Ekrem behind you in the group of people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So Ekrem was taken from the group first and then soon after Sejdo was also taken, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not understand it. Yes, the first one to be taken out was Ismet and I saw him. I did not see who pulled him out; and then after that Ekrem was pulled out and then after Ekrem, Sejdo was pulled out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: As I understood it, you also said that Redzep Foric was also taken out, yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was taken out before I approached that spot, before Ekrem and before Sejdo. He was taken out with Ismet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Just so that we are clear about it, first of all, Ismet and Foric are seen by you on the side of the road standing, having been taken out of the column, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not Ismet Foric, Redzep Foric.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The two people, Ismet Karabasic and Foric Redzep ---

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: -- were both taken out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, they were taken out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But you did not see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw them, but I did not see when they were taken out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The next person who was taken out of the column you said that you saw being taken, and that was Ekrem?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ekrem, yes. As I approached, Ekrem was the first one taken out after Ismet and Redzo. Redzo has been pulled out before and I did not see who pulled him out, and then in front of my eyes Ekrem was taken out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: After Ekrem you also saw Sejdo being taken out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann has already referred you to a statement that you made last year concerning what took place on this occasion. Do you remember him asking you questions about that earlier this morning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I have here a copy of that statement in your own language that has been translated. Your Honour, I put this before the witness at this stage. There is a copy also for the Prosecution. (Statement handed to the witness). This is a statement that has been provided as a translation from that statement that was originally taken through an interpreter and put into English. You can see that on the first page it contains the details about you, your name and who was present when you were questioned. Miryana Chok was your interpreter. Do you remember her?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember who it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If you turn over the page, you will see there that your statement starts with details about your address and your background, the fact that you have been in the JNA, and then what happened ---

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was in the Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: -- on 24th May 1992, can you see that? On the third page of the statement, if you turn over, can you see the passage that begins, "We left the village of Vidovici and began to travel towards Kozarac"? It is the third paragraph on that page 3. Would you like to read that to yourself for a moment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To myself only?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Just looking at what you said on that occasion, you said that your two brothers, Ismet and Ekrem, were ahead of you at the front of the column with their families, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is not right. Ekrem was with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You also said, "Although I did not see them being picked out of the line with my own eyes" -----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see when Ismet and Redzo were taken out. I did not see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that is what you say, but I would like to continue through this statement because you do mention there Redzep Foric, but you say that you were told by Ajka Karabasic what had happened, that Ismet and Ekrem had been picked out from the column, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, this is not, this is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I just want at this stage to confirm what you said at that time. "I saw my two brothers Ismet and Ekrem standing to the right with their hands against the wall of the store that sells chicken"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw them there only when Ekrem was also taken out and he was taken up to Ismet. That is when I saw both of them there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But did you say also on this occasion that standing with your brothers were two other Muslims whom you recognised? They were Redzep Rasima Foric and Meho Edhema Vujkanovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Would you like to just look at your statement there? Perhaps you would like to turn back to page 3 because in this statement here you do mention Redzep Foric, do you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do mention Redzep Foric but we simply cannot agree. I mentioned Redzep Foric as I was passing by the kiosk. I am simply listing people who already were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, and you in this statement here at this time said that he was already standing there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was standing as I was passing by them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: With Meho Edhema Vujkanovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Mujkanovic with an "M", with an "M" rather than "V".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, there is a spelling mistake here and it is a "V" instead of an "M", is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It is not a question, according to this statement, of you muddling up Redzep Foric and Ekrem, is it, because you have already got Ekrem standing by the kiosk?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
