utterances.text: No, I think that the person who interrogated me simply did not put the sequence correctly. I said who was there when they were there, and this is what I said when I was passing by. I mean, as I was passing by they were already all there, and that is the mistake that was made.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Because what I suggest to you is that you did not see Dule Tadic pick out anyone from that column of people, that he was not there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see him pick out Ismet and Redzep, I did not see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You have told the court today that he was dressed -- this was Dule Tadic -- in camouflage uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, a uniform of many colours, yes, I did say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Why did you say in this statement that he was dressed in civilian clothes? If you turn to page 4 -----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remembered it later. I was so depressed and then I remembered, then I recalled how he was dressed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So you agree that you have said on an earlier occasion that he was dressed in civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did say that, but later on I simply regained my memory and I remembered it. At first I did think it was a civilian uniform, but it is not a civilian uniform, some kind of military uniform. I know that some people in Kozarac also had some kind of uniform, something of many colours and the like, and I have always thought it to be some kind of civilian uniform, but it is not. I was wrong. It was a military uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you recollect any other Serbs other than Borovnica and Tadic ---

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I cannot.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: -- who were -----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot. I cannot.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Because they were not just on their own, were they? Were there others with them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were military.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But were there other people who were not military who were there at this place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: None others except for us that were moving in the column, the civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were Tadic and Borovnica with any others in a group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see that, because they were standing each on his own, one on one side and the other one on the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So you cannot name any other people there who were around in that place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, we will have that translation that you have prepared, the statement that was given to the Prosecutor by this witness, we will have that marked for identification purposes as Defence 14, just so that the record will be straight.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am much obliged, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Do you have redirect?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Mr. Karabasic, would you look for me, please, at the Defence document that you were just shown, 14, and would you go to the fourth page? Can you find the fourth page of that? The numbers are down at the very bottom. Do you see right at the bottom it says No. 4? Would you count down 14 lines from the very top, would you just count down the numbers 14 lines from the top, would you just count them down, and when you have got to No. 14, tell me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sure --"I am not sure but I think that Dule Tadic was carrying an automatic rifle and that he was dressed in civilian clothes. Now I am not sure even of what I had on me that day. As we were approaching, my son Sejdo" ---

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: If you just ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- was walking on my right side.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The record will reflect the witness is reading now from Defence 14.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes. If I just repeat the English version to you, just so that we can pick up precisely the quote? Would you listen and look at what I have just shown you in the transcript and does it read to this effect: "I am not sure but I think Dule Tadic was carrying an automatic rifle and was dressed in civilian clothes. I am not even sure right now exactly what it was that I was wearing on that day".

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No further questions, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: I wonder if you might ask the witness for my benefit was it Enver or Emir Karabasic that was, he said, the very good friend of Tadic? That was right at the beginning of his evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: You heard his Honour's question; can you tell us whether it was Enver or Emir Karabasic that was the good friend?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Emir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Could you tell me then what the relationship is between Emir Karabasic and yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We have the same surname but we are not related at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any additional questions, Mr. Niemann?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection to Mr. Karabasic being permanently excused?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Sir, you are permanently excused. You may leave. Thank you for coming.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, would you call your next witness, please

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. The Prosecution's next witness is Uzeir Besic.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I have timed the Prosecution. You have listed Mr. Karabasic for three to four hours and you took an hour and 11 minutes. Maybe that explains why the next witness is not standing out there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Perhaps while we are waiting, I might ask one question really of counsel and it is this: Mr. Karabasic was asked was he a member of the TO and then Reserve service. I must say from previous evidence I had thought that there was the JNA and it was split into active duty and reserve. I did not realise the TO was also divided. I do not think that last witness could have answered it, but it might be clarified whether there was a reserve also in the TO.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will myself check it because my understanding is that some members were reserve, but I would like to confirm it before I answer your Honour on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Thank you. ^^ MR. UZEIR BESIC was called

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Sir, would you take the oath that is before you, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You may be seated. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Sir, what is your name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Uzeir Besic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where were you born, Mr. Besic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What year were you born?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What is your nationality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you grow up in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In what part of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Besici

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Besici is a portion of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It is beyond, just beyond, the mosque up toward Mrakovica, up toward the mountain?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I wonder if we might show a portion of what I believe is Exhibit 195 -- in any event, the technicians know the portion of that particular exhibit -- for the purposes of seeing if we might point out where Besici is located? Sir, I would ask you to run the video through and see if you recognise first the general area that is shown. (The video was played)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can recognise some of these things.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you see the river below the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I do. This is Besici.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can we continue, please, for a moment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you see this structure or a kiosk, the checkpoint. Can we stop for a moment, please? Did you see that structure we just passed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Is that directly across from the Mutnik Mosque?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can we continue, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you recognise what is shown on the video now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What is this building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can we stop here, please? Do you see the white building we are approaching now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What building was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The youth centre, this was not there. This was not here before.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When you say "this" are you referring to the small structure on the right side of the screen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, this structure here. The Local Commune, Kozarac Youth Centre. There was a kiosk here. Now it has gone.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can we return to reverse the video for a moment and return to the portion where we began? Can we start it forward again? Mr. Besic, can you ask us to stop the video when we get the best view of Besici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here, yes, that is fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: All right. Can we continue just a little further? There is a panning shot which may show a larger portion of the hills?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can you stop here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Is Besici the portion depicted in front or further toward the hills?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Up there, higher towards the hills.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you. What nationalities lived in Besici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Approximately how large was the village or hamlet of Besici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, there were up to 80 households. I would not be able to say exactly, but roughly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you attend primary school in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you walk to school every day from Besici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How long a walk was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, say 15 minutes or so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After primary school, did you train as a machinist, train to become a machinist?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was not a machinist.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you do some kind of work related training after primary school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: First I worked in Ivanic-Grad. Then I went to do my military service. I returned from the army to Ivanic-Grad, to the company I worked for, and then I was trained in the Dvor Na Uni.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you recall approximately when you began working in Ivanic-Grad?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I began in 1980.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you a painter for a firm in Ivanic-Grad?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Ivanic-Grad is in Croatia near Zagreb, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, near Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How often did you return home to Kozarac when you were working there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Every weekend.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You also told us that you performed compulsory service with the JNA; what year was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From '82 to '83.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In the JNA were you in the infantry for three months and then worked in the laundry service after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In 1986 did you begin work for a construction firm in Ljubljana in Slovenia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How often did you come home at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, every fortnight or once a month or so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In 1990 did you return home to Kozarac when the firm you were working for went bankrupt?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you then stay in Besici until the attack on Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you know Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How long have you known him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ever since I was a school boy.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was your school close to his house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you see him regularly in town while you were growing up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: By and large.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was he a well-known person in town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: For what reason?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, because of karate and he practised karate, he was around.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you have friends who trained with him or learned from him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you sometimes watch Dule Tadic and your friends train?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, sometimes, sometimes -- very seldom however.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Is Dule Tadic your age?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Is he older or younger?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Older.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you have a brother about his age?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did your brother know Dule Tadic well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, generally speaking, he knew him better than I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When you and Dule Tadic passed each other on the streets in Kozarac, would you greet each other, say "hello"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it was mostly in company when I would be with some friends of mine, and when they would be more people that he knew, then we would greet each other, but we never socialised. We never went to some place together.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was he married?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was his wife's name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mira.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What did she do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe she was a nurse.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did they have children?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How many?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think they had two.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Back in Kozarac, do you remember what size man Dule Tadic was? Can you describe his physical size and build?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Tadic was of medium height. He was taller than I am, rather sturdy and so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did he sometimes have a beard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did he sometimes not have a beard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sometimes he was without a beard, sometimes with a beard -- mostly with a beard.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, I would like now to ask you a few questions about the period of time between the takeover of Prijedor by Serbian authorities and the attack on Kozarac. Had Serbian military forces set up roadblocks on the main road between Kozarac and Prijedor and between Kozarac and Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think they did set up roadblocks when they took over the power in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were Serb military forces and equipment positioned in the area of Kozarac during that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were positioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did Serbian authorities send a message to the people of Kozarac to surrender all their weapons and to accept the Serbian flag?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were negotiations to have the people surrender and disarm, to have the Territorial Defence and police disarm, to give, surrender our arms to the Serbs and in that case we would not have any problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did Muslim leaders from Kozarac attempt to negotiate some sort of peaceful solution with Serbian authorities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they went to negotiations, to peaceful negotiations. I am not really well informed about this, but I hear that they went to negotiate and to have the problem solved peacefully but they did not manage to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When did the Serbian attack on Kozarac begin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On May 24th.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: About what time of day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was around 2 o'clock in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Despite the gathering of troops and equipment, despite the ultimatum by Serbian authorities to hand over weapons and accept the Serbian flag, did the attack come as a surprise to you and to your family and friends?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it was a surprise, yes, something was expected, but nobody really expected an attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was Kozarac prepared to defend itself militarily?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You mentioned there was a local police force and a TO. Had there been some guarding of local institutions before the attack occurred?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was TO, naturally, and police; there were some watchers, guards.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: During the period of time shortly before the attack, was there an attempt to mobilize the local TO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, there was. There was mobilization, but we had nothing else, nothing came out of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Had you heard any talk about any individual attempting to organise some kind of defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were individuals who tried to do something but all in all they did not succeed. It was not possible to defend Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After the attack on Kozarac occurred, did you see any indication that anyone had managed to put together a military defence for the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where were you when the attack began?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was at home in Besici.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Who were you with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was with my family -- father, mother, wife, children.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How did the attack begin, with what kind of weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It started with shelling.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After the shelling began, what did you and your family do, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We went to a nearby basement because we did not have a basement in our house. So ----

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did other people from Besici gather at the neighbour's basement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mostly they were in the basement. That was the first refuge they sought out; whoever could find some kind of a place to hide.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you stay that night in Besici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How steady or intensive was the shelling that day of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was very heavy shelling.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was Besici shelled?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mostly not, or to a smaller degree.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The next morning did the shelling continue?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you and your family leave Besici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we went up there towards the mountains, towards the forest and other people from Kozarac, nearby towns, were joining us. We were mostly fleeing towards the forest. We were looking for a place where we could be saved.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You indicated that you and other people from Kozarac and nearby towns were joining you. How many people gathered in the forest, if you can estimate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A lot of people were going into the forest, hundreds, but there were many people, many people. They were coming from Kozarac and from other parts, other parts of Kozarac, from Besici and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were they gathering in the same place or in different parts of the forest?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were not all in the same group, but there were large groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: These were men, women, children, old people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were women, elderly, children, everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What ethnic group were these people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you and your family stay in the forest on that night, the day after the attack began?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The next morning did you and your wife and children return to Besici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you return to the forest briefly that morning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I returned because people were leaving the forest and then coming back, and then somebody saw my mother, said that she remained up there, she could not come down, and I went back to fetch her and I brought her back into Besici.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was happening in Besici on that morning, on Tuesday morning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Somebody came and informed, somebody came from Kozarac, I do not remember who it was, and told us that we can go downward in columns and that people are going down there to surrender; there were women, children in the columns and that the column was walking with a white flag in front of it. But there great panic arose among people because we heard that they were taking out men, capable men, and shooting them, so that I sent my wife and children there and I myself went back.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When the people went down into Kozarac to surrender, how did they indicate they were surrendering?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They indicated by the great column that had a white flag in front of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What about your parents, did they decide to go down with the column and surrender?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My parents remained at home. They did not want to leave their house as well as some other people.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did they hope that things would be all right for older people such as them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were hoping that nobody would touch them. They were in their own house. They did not want to go. They remained in their house.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you later find out what happened to the people who remained in Besici such as your parents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I heard when I was in Keraterm camp that my father was shot.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you find out what happened to your mother?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My mother was with my aunt and another woman. They remained there. I heard that she was wounded and then I don't know what happened to her afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you leave Besici and return to the forest?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were there still people in the forest?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: As many as before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there were less.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were some of those people preparing to surrender?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some were preparing to go and surrender and some remained, continued to stay in the forest and were making plans where to go what would be the best thing to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was this mass of people separating into smaller groups?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were mostly separating into groups, into smaller groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How were these groups chosen, friends, relatives? What was the basis for forming a group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Generally the group was formed based on relatives; the group was formed out of relatives, friends, acquaintances.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you become part of such a group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were the people in your group relatives and friends of yours?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were relatives and friends.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How many people in your group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were 12 of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did the others decide to remain in the forest for the same reason you had because of fear of what might happen to the Muslim men who surrendered?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What did the men in your group hope to do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were thinking about -- we thought that they would not get to the forest that fast. We were thinking about what we ought to do and we mostly thought to go to Croatia through Kozara.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did any of you have weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How long did you and your friends remain in the woods?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Until 31st May.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: During that time until 31st May what were you doing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were in the forest. We were looking for food.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you hiding?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we were hiding in the forest, sleeping there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now on 31st May did some members of your group go to try to find some food?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, four from our group because we decided that we needed to find more food and try and go to Croatia, and eight of us remained in the forest.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: During that day were the eight of you spotted by Serbian forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did they fire at you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they fired first at us, they noticed us, and we were frightened in the forest and we scattered away through the forest. They were calling at us to come out and not be afraid because they would not hurt us, they would not do anything to us and not to worry.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did any of the members of your group respond to that call to come out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, a friend of mine frightened, we were all frightened, we were all in panic and this was the first encounter of that kind that we ever had, he started yelling, "Don't shoot, don't shoot, we are coming out", and he ran out into the road and this was by a road, by a place called Kadina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What did the rest of you do after your friend ran out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We came, all of us came out.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did the Serbian forces take your documents and valuables?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we came out the forest a group of Serbian soldiers came before us and they said, they told us to raise our arms up there and ordered us to empty our pockets and take out anything that we had there, documents, money, to take out anything that was in the pockets.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of these Serbian soldiers as local Serbs, people from the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not at that moment, I did not recognise anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did any of them know or recognise any members of your group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, one of them recognised a friend of mine and he called him by his name and said: 'Oh, so you are here too. You'll get what you deserve."

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where did the Serb soldiers take your group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They took us in front of a house that was underneath Kozarac hills, and when we came there there was a lot of Serb army there. In front of that house there was a woman, an owner of the house, Jasna, that I know and on one bench there was a man with a beard, with a long beard, and he was not in a camouflage uniform. On his head he had a fur hat and on the fur hat he had a Kokarda sign.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was he in a kind of Chetnik uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that was a Chetnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What did the Serb soldiers do with you and the other members of your group at that point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They tied us, they tied us with some kind of a rope, and then we lay down in front of that house. I was third from the beginning. This is how we were lying down and they provoked us. They were insulting us, cursing us. They did not beat us, but they were pointing weapons towards us and aiming at us.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You mentioned that the soldiers were insulting you and cursing you. Were they using ethnic insults?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, those were ethnic insults. They were cursing our Turkish mothers, Muslim mothers.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were they also using the word "balija"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you singled out from the others?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At one point the woman, the owner of that house, was ordered to go into the house and her daughter-in-law stayed there and then she started crying and then she joined her into the house. She went into the house and then later on a Serbian soldier came and hit me with his leg and he told me to get up, and I got up and he told me, "You will come with us towards Kozarac", and I was frightened. I did not feel like going and I did not feel like separating, like being separated from my group. I was afraid. He said: "Come on, why don't you start? What are you waiting for?" So a group of my relatives and friends remained there and I just turned towards them and they looked, those friends and relatives of mine looked at me. Then I had to start walking.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: As you set off into the forest, did you hear anything, any sounds, coming from the area that you had just left?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, when I started walking with them after about 50 or so metres I heard screams, shooting. I immediately figured out and I thought, oh, they shot them all, and I was thinking, what shall I do with myself? How will I go on? I just said to myself, if they start doing something to me, I will start running and they can shoot me if they want.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you or any other friends or relatives ever see any of those men alive again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serbian men?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The members of your group, your friends and family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not understand the question well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you ever see any of the members of your group, your friends and family, alive again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Later on in 1993 after you had left Bosnia, did someone approach you and indicate that pictures had been taken by someone of bodies in the general area where you had been?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were those pictures presented to you in 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you able to recognise the bodies depicted in those photos from the clothing the persons were wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I have these four photographs marked Exhibit 226, A, B, C and D? Sir, can I ask you to look at those photographs and tell us if those are the photographs you were just referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, those are those pictures.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: May those be placed on the monitor, please? Are those four members of your group, Mr. Besic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can the photograph be moved, there is a glare on quite a portion of it. Can we see the next photograph, please? Is this another member of your group, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The next photograph, please? Is this the sixth member of your group, another one of your friends or relatives?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The last photograph, please. Sir, do you know exactly when these pictures were taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The pictures were taken after, after a month I think, a month after this event.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Is this the seventh member of your group, another friend or relative?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender 226 A through D for admission.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 226 A, B, C and D will be admitted. We will stand in recess until 2.30.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Your Honours, I just wanted to make reference to the witness list and indicate to the court and foreshadow there may be some variation in the order. Witness No. 26 on the list is from North America. He has had difficulty with passports, so it does not look as though he will be here on time to give evidence as we expected. Witness No. 27 is the ID witness that we have spoken of and have pushed further back down the list now because of the ID issue which is to be resolved. So, we will drop him from that order.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Where would you put 27?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: It is a bit hard to guess at this stage, but either late next week, that would be Wednesday of next week, or he may fall over to the period after July, depending on how we are going then, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: So you will not call witness 27 after Mr. Besic?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, your Honours. We will wait until that issue of ID has resolved itself.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: So your next witness will be 24, then 25 and then 26 -- no, you are not certain about 26, when you will call him, because of the passport problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, he has passport problems.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: When will you know about that? When will you know whether that has been worked out?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: This is the hands of the Government that issues the passports, your Honours, and we are uncertain as to when that will be resolved.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: What are we going to do? When would you be able to tell the Defence? I am really concerned about the Defence. They want to know because they want to be able to cross-examine. You will have 27, 24, 25 and then what happens?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: 25 and then ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Then either 26 or 30?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Then we go on to the next one after 25 will be now No. 30.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Then 31.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: How much lead time will you have regarding 26 in terms of the passport situation?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: He was spoken to yesterday and his application is still being processed. We have spoken to officials in the government where he lives and asked them to expedite it as quickly as they can. It is really a day-to-day issue as to whether it will be cleared. We had hoped that the issue would be resolved by now and he would be on his way here and there would be no problem, but as of the moment that has not been resolved.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You will tell Defence counsel then the day before you intend to call him?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: At least the day before, no later than the day before, you intend to call 26. So we will leave 26 kind of floating for the moment until you let us know about that. 27, you will be putting after which witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: After the argument on and resolution of the issue on ID.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 27 is the first ID witness. Is there another one that comes up?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Not before.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: When is the next one after 27?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The next witness after 27 or the next ID witness?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there another ID witness after 27 and, if so, what number?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I am not in a position to answer that, your Honour. There are other ID witnesses we are calling, but he is the first ID witness that will come up in these batch of witnesses. We have pushed him back because the issue needs to be resolved before calling him, but there will be others later on. But I am not in a position to answer that yet, your Honour. I will have to go through and check each statement to see which one is ID as opposed to which one is recognition ---

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: -- and I have not done that.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Make sure that we have enough time to resolve the issue then before we hear 27. Maybe tomorrow morning you can tell me when you want to put 27 because, I gather, there are some in between here who are not eyewitnesses -- ID witness problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, all the others are recognition, your Honour. We have worked out a new list to keep us going, so now it will be the same list, except that 26, 27 and 29 at the moment are dropping down, but 28 is still in place and No. 30 and 31 are still in place. I will prepare a new list so it is easy to follow.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 30 and 31 are not ID problems?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, and nor is 28.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: What about 32?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Nor is 32.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. I think we have enough witnesses; we certainly have enough witnesses through this week and probably even Tuesday too before we even get to the ID problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: That is our plan, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Probably we need to talk about the ID problem then on Wednesday. I will talk with the Judges to see if we can come up with a time -- maybe Wednesday morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: One other matter, your Honours, I have had discussion with the Defence and we have agreed amongst ourselves that when we refer to our interpreters, rather than mention their name, we will merely pass the statement to the witness and ask the witness whether that was the interpreter that was present, if that convention is acceptable to the court.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. Mr. Kay and Mr. Wladimiroff, will you do that, avoid mentioning the names of the interpreters?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there anything else?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. Continue with the witness. MR. UZEIR BESIC, recalled.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Mr. Besic, just before the recess you identified the photographs of your friends and families. Can I ask you what ethnic group these people belonged to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You indicated earlier that when the Serbs singled you out and took you off it was for the purpose, they said, of having you direct them to Kozarac. Did they take you all the way into Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where did they stop?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They stopped by the first houses towards the village of Besici.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did they ask you either at that time or earlier where certain parts of Opstina Prijedor were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As we were coming down from the house where we were, a group stayed there, as I have said, and with me climbed down one of the Commanders and part of the army; and their superior asked me where I was born, where I had worked, what I was doing, and I told him. He asked me if I had any children, I told him and then he took out a knife -- I was tied -- and he untied my hands. When we reached the first houses we stopped there and they asked me where the village Rajkovici was, in which direction were Prijedor and Corici. Then they went to a house, a group of soldiers went to a house, and set it on fire. This Commander asked me where would I go if he let me off, and I did not know where to or how. I was frightened out of my wits. Now, by another house there was an old woman and an old man and a boy. So I asked if I could, "Can I stay with them?" and he said, "Do that". They were still there and there they took their positions. I then realised that perhaps he would not kill me, or I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you stay at that house for some time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he told me to stay in that house, but he also said, "Now another round of the army come and I will give them your name so that nothing happens to you". So, then they left and another group of military came. They were wearing SMB uniforms and they had white arm bands. They asked me about my first name and my family name, because this one, the first one, must have told them -- he had a walkie-talkie or something -- that I was there so I was there until right until the 3rd, until the 3rd.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did the other soldiers who came, the ones in the SMB uniform, tell you not to leave, not to try to escape?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, later on as I was in this house with this old man and old woman and this boy, a soldier came and told me not to even try to escape, not to go anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: On your way to this area did you see other Serb soldiers in the region when you were walking from the place where you had left your friends and family to the area of Besici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was in the house until the 3rd and then the orders came to leave that house, myself and that old man, woman and the boy, and they took us towards Rajkovici. We were going to the forest and, as we were coming closer to Rajkovici, there were all Serb soldiers, all one next to the other. They had taken up positions there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You mentioned the 3rd, is that 3rd June?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What kind of village was Rajkovici, that is, what nationality or nationalities lived in Rajkovici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The majority of Rajkovici villagers were Catholics.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So they were a Croat nationality or Croat origin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Croats, Catholics, Bosnian Croats, shall we say.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: During these days did you hear any of the soldiers speaking in a way that indicated they were from outside Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, their accent was different. Their accent was not Bosnian, and that was how I knew they were not local Serbs from local places. However, there were some local ones among them, but I believe from other parts.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When you were taken to Rajkovici, in addition to seeing many soldiers, did you also see another Croat or Muslim captive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, when we arrived in Rajkovici, I saw a boy tied to a tree. He had been wounded and beaten up and was tied to a tree.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Approximately, what age was this boy or young man?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I should say he was my age, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was his condition, his physical condition?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was battered, he was severely beaten up and his leg was injured.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did the soldiers ask you if you knew him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, later I was approached by two Serb policemen and they took me to him and asked me if I knew him. I said "no". Then they asked him if he knew me and he only made a sign with his head to show that he did not. Had I even known him, I would not have been able to recognise him, he was that badly beaten up.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What happened to you after you said that you did not know the young man and he said he did not know you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, then they beat me, soldiers and so .....

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How did they beat you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They kicked me with their feet and the like. I cannot even remember how it was. I only know they beat me. I know I was beaten up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were they saying anything to you, were cursing you, as they were beating you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As they beat me, yes, they did. They cursed at me, my "balija mother" and the like. They were mostly ethnic curses.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When the beating stopped what did they do with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When the beating stopped a Commander of sorts came, I assume he was the Commander, and he told them to untie the one that was tied to a tree, and to tie us with the wire and to put us on a military vehicle -- it was a van or something -- and to take us away somewhere. Before that, they asked, "And what are we to do, what about these two old people?" because there was this old man and the woman -- the old man I knew, the woman I did not -- and they said, "Take them to the forest and kill them because they defended this camp".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was the old couple taken away into the forest?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and they were taken up towards the forest. I heard shots and then we were put in a van and we took off.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Who was put in the van?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Myself, the one who was tied to a tree and the boy that was with those old people who came with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Approximately how old was that person, not the one who had been tied to a tree, but the other young man?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, he was 17 or 16, maybe 18. I would not know exactly. He was young.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did the van in which the three of you were transported have windows?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were windows.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you able to see the place where you were taken when you arrived? Were you able to see it and recognise it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, as we rode in that van I saw something. I could turn my head and could see that we were heading towards Prijedor, and when we arrived I realised that we were in the Prijedor barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Is that the JNA barracks, by the way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the former JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When you arrived at the Prijedor JNA barracks, where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we got off the van we were taken to a building. We entered a corridor and the one who had driven us there took us in. I do not know what they were, policemen or what, and said, "There they are", and he point and said that, "This one had a machine gun, and beat him", and they started to beat me. They were beating me with their foot and with their batons.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When you were taken inside this building and into a hallway, were you and the other two placed in some portion of the hallway?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we first came into that hallway and I remember there was a room there, a toilet and we stood there against the wall. Across the hallway, across the corridor, were rooms and we faced the wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was there a portion of the hallway to your right as you faced the wall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, a longish corridor, a longer hallway, as I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were there offices or rooms down the hallway to your right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was there also a portion of hallway to your left as you faced the wall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, there was the exit from the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were the other two young men with you to your right or to your left?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You said the soldiers then started to beat you. Did they say anything to you as they beat you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The common curses.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did they beat you with any objects?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They beat us with police batons.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you remain standing after the beating started?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After the blows I crumbled down on the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What part of your body were they hitting when the beating began?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the beginning around my shoulders, my back.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You say you crumbled down to the floor, in what position were you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I collapsed. I was on my knees and I was by the wall facing the wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was your face facing forward, facing left or facing right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Facing to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After you crumbled to your knees, did the soldiers continue to beat you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were some easier blows, lighter blows, and they were also hitting me with their legs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: As you were down on your knees with your head facing right, did you see anyone coming from an office down the corridor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. While I was on my knees, out of a room which was up there in the corridor, I saw Dule Tadic coming out from a room and walking outside, outside of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Walking in your direction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He was walking towards exit.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How was he dressed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was in camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you see him leave the office and then see him approach toward you down the hall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was walking towards us. He left the room. He was walking towards us, and as he was going out he kicked me a few times with his feet and then he went out. I do not know where he went after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After that what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After that we were untied. Nothing was happening. They were not beating us. They were pretending that nothing happened and they started interrogating us in a room, in an office.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: During the course of the interrogation did they ask you about weapons and arms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they asked me about arms, where I was, what I was doing, and the like; what kind of an arm -- what kind of a weapon I had.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What did you tell them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the person that was interrogating me told me it is better to admit that I had a rifle, so I had to admit that I had a weapon and then, finally, I signed a statement which said that I participated in arm uprising -- armed uprising against Serbian people.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After being presented with this document and at the conclusion of the interrogation where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After that interrogation, the three of us -- a car came, the Yugo car came with two policemen and they took us to Keraterm camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: They took you and the two others who had been with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When you arrived at Keraterm were the three of you confronted by any uniformed Serb?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we came to Keraterm these two policemen that brought us and drove us in, gave us, turned us over to a soldier whose name was Zoran Zigic. When I say "Zoran Zigic", I did not know this person before, but I heard his name mentioned in the camp afterwards, and he stood there and greeted us there with some other soldiers, guards.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I ask that Z3, 30-9 -- I am told we would be better off placing this on the elmo, so if I could have this photograph marked for identification as Prosecution 227? Mr. Besic, do you recognise what is shown in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Does that depict the general area where you were with Zoran Zigic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it depicts, this is -- there are a scale. I think that this is a scale. I have never been in this facility before.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender this 227 for admission.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 227 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If I may have this marked as Exhibit 228? Mr. Besic, does this photograph more clearly depict the area you were speaking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I would tender 228, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Which photograph is that, which number?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 228 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: May that be placed on the monitor, please? Your Honour, I can show 227. It is just a ----

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: If it is an exhibit, we should see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sure. This is 227, your Honour. For the record, the exhibit now on the monitor is 228. (To the witness): When Zigic confronted the three of you in this area, what happened? What did he first ask or do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we came there by him he asked us what nationality we were. We told him we were Muslim. Then he ordered, he ordered us, "Let's see how the Muslims pray to the God". So we had to show him. Then later he said, "Let's take" -- he told us to take our underwear off so that he can see if we were circumcised and if we were not that he would do that. So we had to do at that as well. Then he beat us with his feet. I think he also had a rifle and he beat us with his -- with the butt of the rifle and then he sent us to a room. I think it was called No. 1. There was already full of detainees.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did Zigic tell you to stay in a particular part of room No. 1?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, straight at the door he told us: "Well, you will stay here".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Later that same day were other prisoners brought to Keraterm and put in the same cell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the same day and sometime afterwards, a little bit later and then came full of inmates and later we heard that they were from Ljubija near Prijedor. Those were Croats and Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How many Croats and Muslims were brought from Ljubija that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were 10. I think there were 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did Zigic confront them when they arrived as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he treated them the same way. I saw from behind the corner where I was standing that he beat them and then he brought them upstairs and put in the room where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The translation says "upstairs"; were you on the ground floor or in an upstairs area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was ground floor but when I say "up" there, I meant from the scales towards the room where I was, close to the room where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You also said earlier there were many other prisoners in room No. 1 or cell No. 1 when you arrived; what nationality were those prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were mostly Muslims and there were some Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Over the next two weeks were you and others taken from room No. 1 repeatedly and beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, regularly. We were regularly taken out by Zigic and we were beaten by him, but he was also taking out other people. In front of the door he would order us to sing the songs and he would beat us at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Who was taken out with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Other than myself it was -- they took out the guy that came with me from Rajkovici who was tied up there and others that came after me to Keraterm from Ljubija.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you recall whether they also took out the young man who came with you from Besici to Rajkovici to the barracks and then to Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he was not taken out.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You said that you and the others were forced to sing. What kinds of songs were you forced to sing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We sang Serbian songs, and then Zigic just wanted to play with us, and we sang some, are extremist song, just like if we were extremists, and he was ordering us to sing the extremists songs and he would order us to sing this song: "We will beat JNA and Krajina will collapse and Alija is our leader", so he would be standing in front of us and we would be singing and he would say: "Well, who is going to collapse?"

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did Zigic force the prisoners to hit one another?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he would force us.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You also indicated that other prisoners besides you and the people you mentioned who were called out with you would be called out from the room and beaten. How often did this occur?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It would occur mostly when Zigic's shift was on. He would call out people in the evening, take the people out, beat them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How long did you stay in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot tell exactly, but around 14 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where were you taken after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After that a police car, a police van, came and there were 13 of us called out and we were taken to Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When you arrived at Omarska were guards there to take you from the police car, the police van?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. When we came to Omarska there were guards there. We came out one by one and we were told to raise our arms behind our neck and go into garage one by one. Then we lined up and when we entered the hangar, as we were walking they were hitting us, beating us and took us to the room No. 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you remain in that room until you were interrogated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the room No. 15 I was, I stayed there until I was interrogated.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where were you interrogated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were interrogated on the floor by the restaurant, in a room there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was that on the ground floor or on the upper floor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Upper floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you know the person who conducted the interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was interrogated by Radakovic, the head of the National Park in Kozarac. I knew him in Kozara, National Park in Kozara. I knew him a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did Radakovic know that you had previously been in the JNA barracks and in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think he knew. I also told him everything. I told him what happened, how I got there and what happened up until then, up until that moment when I was interrogated.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you beaten during the interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: First, I was interrogated and then after that Radakovic did not beat me, but I was beaten by the guard that brought me to the room where I was interrogated.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How were you beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was beaten so that I had to kneel and they would beat me from up there with the batons. They would beat me on my back and on my kidney area.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: At the end of this interrogation and beating, were you presented with something to sign?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After that interrogation, I came out to pista and after a certain time I was called out by a guard and he took me back there to Radakovic. They read to me everything that I told them, everything that occurred during the interrogation, and then I signed that statement and went back to pista.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The pista is the open space between the restaurant building and the hangar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That is a concrete area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you stay there during the day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, during the day we were there. In the evening, we would mostly go to the restaurant and sometimes we would sleep outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was there any protection from the sun during the day for the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there was no protection. Those detainees who would get to the hangar first there was just more shade there, but otherwise we had to sit in the sun, in the scorching sun.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Approximately how many prisoners were on the pista, if you can estimate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not hear the translation well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I was just wondering if you could give us any estimate of how many prisoners were on the pista?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the pista maybe, according to my estimate, around 300, 500. I do not know exactly, but I know that pista was always full.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I wonder if I might at this time show some brief video footage depicting that general area of Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is that from an exhibit that is already in evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: To my knowledge, it is not from an exhibit that is already in evidence; it is from footage which the Defence has seen.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That will be marked, what do you propose, 229?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: 229, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, does this show the pista looking toward the restaurant building with the cameraman's back to the hangar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What is now shown on the screen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Does this now show the pista from the other side, that is, looking at the hangar with the cameraman's back to the restaurant building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Does this now show the pista with the cameraman standing in the general area of the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender Exhibit 229.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 229 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: This might be an appropriate time to indicate to the court that the footage previously shown I had indicated was from Exhibit 195; I am advised it is actually from Exhibit 107.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That was the film; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes. It showed the area of Besici.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: During the day, Mr. Besic, how did prisoners stay on the pista? How did they sit and, if so, in what position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, we would sit, sometimes we would sit, sometimes we would lie on our stomach. If we were sitting we would be, we would turn our backs to the restaurant. If we were lying, then we would face the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You said when you were sitting you would turn your backs to the restaurant; did that mean you would face the hangar when you were sitting? Which direction did you face when you were sitting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If we were sitting, we would face the restaurant, if we were sitting; and if we were lying on our stomachs, we would turn and watch and face the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were there particular occasions when prisoners were made to lie down instead of sit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mostly we were ordered to lie down. They would yell, "Lie down", and if something, if there was an incident, something would happen, if somebody was carried out from interrogation, then in order not to have us see something, not to have us see what is happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When prisoners were sitting were they generally discouraged by the guards from looking around?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, if something was happening, we would not be sitting down. If they were beating somebody, or carrying them out, carry them out from interrogation, because people were carried out from interrogation, beaten up or they would be dead, in that case we would have to lie down on our stomachs so that we would not see that, or if they were in a bad mood, if the guards were in a bad mood, then sometimes we had to lie for several hours in the sun.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: While you were on the pista did you ever see Dule Tadic in Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: While I was on the pista I saw Dule Tadic once.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where were you sitting at the time? Can I ask you to take that pointer on the table and point to the position, the approximate position, in which you were sitting when you saw Dule Tadic on Exhibit 130, the model?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I was sitting here more or less. (Indicated on the model). Here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In what position were you sitting, not the position relative to the camp, but just how were you sitting? On your knees? Sitting down?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were sitting normally with my knees up, I think. I mean, like this, like everybody else, so that my knees were up, up to here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In which direction were you facing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was facing in the direction of the building where the interrogations went on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Before you saw Dule Tadic did anything bring your attention to the area where you finally saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
