utterances.text: Yes, I was drawn, the attention or, rather, I heard some yells and shouts of some inmates or some detainees who were behind the building where the interrogations took place. I heard some yells, some screams, some loud cries, so that I simply looked in that direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can you point to the general area where you heard those sounds coming from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The yelling came here, from this side, from here. (The witness indicated on the model).

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Then what did you next see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After that I saw the inmates coming in -- coming out. They had already come out and there was Dule Tadic with some soldiers. I do not know how many of them there were. All of a sudden, we were ordered, "Lie down", and we have already learned that "Lie down", we knew that it was a sign to go down in the prone position and so that was that. Others to the right in the white house, those who were coming out from the other side, from this other building, they also came and lied down next to me in a line.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So that before you took the position you were ordered to take lying down on the pista, you saw Dule Tadic and some soldiers come from the area behind the restaurant building along with prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can you point out where he was when you first saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first time I glimpsed him he was somewhere here. (The witness indicated on the model).

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Did you see that, Mr. Wladimiroff?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Would you point it out again?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, if you could point it out once more?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After you took the position laying down on the pista, the prisoners who had been brought from around the corner of the restaurant building came to the area near you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can you show us again where you were at that time and where the prisoners were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, here, more or less. All this was filled to capacity with inmates and I was here; and when those came that I already mentioned, they moved in here around here next to me, and each one took up some position.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So the prisoners who had come from the area behind the restaurant building took a position to your right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you hear sounds coming from those prisoners? You may sit down, Mr. Besic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean those lying next to me?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The prisoners who had come from the area of the restaurant who were lying to your right, did you hear sounds coming from them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were lying around me. There were, I think, half cries of pain, moaning, and as I was lying down I raised my head a little bit. I saw they were being beaten, that they were kicking them, jumping on them and Dule Tadic was hitting them, jumping on them and such like; and then orders came for them to stand up and to move on and they went towards the white house and entered. I could not see whether they all entered it, or whether some went on and I saw them going after them, but I saw them entering and what happened to those people then, I do not know. I knew surnames of many of them. There were Alic's, Foric's and others. I never heard about those people again, whether they were still alive or not; at any rate, I never saw them again.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When Dule Tadic was jumping on these prisoners and such, did you look more than once while the beating was taking place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I looked two to three times.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How long did the beating last?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it lasted not long but, say, I do not know, I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were some of the prisoners beaten so badly they had to be carried off?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, some were so beaten up that they had to be carried away. I remember a young man who was screaming and others had to carry him, I mean, inmates who were not that badly beaten had to carry him, and he was yelling, "Please do kill me". I think that his backbone was broken.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you moved from the pista within a few days of this incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A few days later I moved to room 26.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you remain in room 26 until most of the prisoners in the camp were moved from Omarska in early August?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I stayed in room 26 until the closure of the Omarska camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you taken to Manjaca or Trnopolje when most of the other prisoners were removed from Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I stayed for some more time with another 100 or so inmates in Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When most of the prisoners went to Manjaca and Trnopolje, were their names called off of lists before they boarded buses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were calls out, I think some were called out. I believe there were two groups. One group was taken towards the buses and another group that went to Trnopolje later on, they were sitting on the pista. Depending on whose name is called out and then he would be told, "You go here" and "You go there". I believe there were two groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were there many prisoners, that is, were there many names called for people who did not respond?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, most of them, when they would call out names they also called out the names who had disappeared from Omarska camp, those who had been taken away or been killed or died as a result of beatings. They themselves did not know whom they had killed and what they had been doing. So these people still featured on the lists of those alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How many prisoners stayed in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember exactly, but I think 182 or 162. I cannot tell you exactly. At any rate, that is when the Red Cross came in the Omarska camp and put our names on record.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What happened that night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That night when everybody had left, one group had left to Manjaca, another one later on to Trnopolje, and we stayed behind, we were all frightened; "Everybody has left and we are still here; God knows what will happen to us". Later on, we were in a room, we were put in a room behind the canteen or, rather, below the building where we had been interrogated; and after a while a big trailer truck arrived. Several guards came and said that some 10 men had to come out and unload something, and we went there and began unloading that trailer. We saw military cots and we realised then that something would happen to us, so we unloaded those cots and took them into the room and put them around. That is how we spent that night.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So beds arrived that night and were assembled?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we did not sleep at all. We were putting them up, assembling them, putting them in order; and as the dawn broke out a Commander came called Brk -- I believe his nickname was "Brk" -- and he ordered us all outside the hall and said, "Today journalists will come", and we were accommodated there so as not to say anything about what I am telling you. He told us, "You may not say that you have been here for more than 20 days. You have to say that you have accommodation here, you have beds, that you eat twice a day, that you were not beaten", and so on and so forth. True enough, that day we ate twice. We went to get our food and there was a lot of food. Each of us was given half a loaf of bread so that we really ate enough, but there was too much food, and since we were all famished some of them got sick -- I was one of those -- after all that food; and then we had to clean up those rooms where the detainees had been kept to conceal any track of them, any trace, any sign, that could show something.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: During the cleaning were prisoners ordered to clean up any or as many traces of blood from the various rooms as they were able?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the orders were to clean up everything that could be indicating a murder or something like that. Some people went to clean houses and I was cleaning the hangar. There was a wire and there were still some jackets or sneakers or shoes and things like that had been left behind and we had all to put them together. There was a large container. We were loading this in and then we took some hoses from the water supply, and then we washed it all away, and near the -- in the white house we saw that there were some lockers and they were all removing them; presumably, they were trying to hide traces, holes of bullets or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, in the translation we received it said in the white house there were "locks"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Lockers".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you. It has been straightened out. You said that Brk told the prisoners that journalists would be coming that day. Do you know whether or not other journalists had come before most of the prisoners had been removed from Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard those journalists were there but I did not see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did any among the 160 to 180 people who remained in the camp, did any women remain in camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were five women.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were they shown to the journalists or were they hidden from the journalists?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Whenever journalists or the Red Cross came, they would be taken away somewhere and hidden, so that they were never shown in Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, you just explained a little bit of what conditions were like in Omarska after most of the prisoners were taken to Trnopolje or Manjaca and journalists were permitted in. What were conditions like in Omarska before that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before that the conditions were terrible. We did not receive enough food or enough water to drink. We were dirty. There was no hygiene. We had lice, dysentery.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were prisoners regularly beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Were they beaten after I stayed behind or before that? I did not quite understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Before most of the prisoners were taken from Omarska, were there regular beatings of prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were regular beatings.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did those beatings take place when prisoners went to eat, for example?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, when we would go to the restaurant we went in groups of 30. Sometimes there would be no beatings but more often there were beatings.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were there women in camp in addition to the men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where were they held?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Women, during the day time, they were usually in the restaurant. They sat there. When food was distributed, some of them worked in the kitchen and, I do not know, cleaning something.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were prisoners called out from the various rooms at night and beaten or killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. People were called out, taken out, some returned, some never returned.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was the nationality of the prisoners in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslims, most of them, and there were some Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was the nationality of the guards and the Commanders of the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The guards and Commanders, I think they were all Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was the ethnic group, for example, of Mr. Radakovic who interrogated you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think he was a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, I would ask you to look around the courtroom and tell us if Dule Tadic is in court today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can you point out where he is sitting, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Over there is that individual.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What is he wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He wears a suit, a tie. He is nicely dressed, clean shaven. His hair is in order.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: May the record reflect the identification of the accused?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Why do you not ask him a few more questions? There are a lot of people in here dressed in suits and ties, are there not, cleanly shaven, nicely dressed -- I am looking at a law clerk.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: He was pointing at the same time, your Honour, so I can have him do it again. Sir, can you point to Dule Tadic once more, please, the person you indicated was wearing the suit and tie?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is this person sitting over there between two policemen. He has a green suit, a tie, mottled, and he is nicely, cleanly shaven and looks very neat. That is that individual.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Besic. You may be seated. Yes, the record will reflect that the witness identified Mr. Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, are you absolutely sure that this is the man who kicked you in the Prijedor JNA barracks and who abused the prisoners on the pista in Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Absolutely sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you sir. Nothing further, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will stand in recess for 20 minutes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, yes. I just would like to raise the matter that was raised by Judge Stephen in relation to the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. I thought you were going to tell us some more about witnesses. Every time we come in and you are standing, I say, "Oh, what are you going to tell me this time?" OK. That is an easy one. Tell us about the Reserve TO.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Territorial Defence, apparently, has a standing staff, a small standing administrative type staff, in each municipality which operates on a permanent basis. The actual manpower of the TO is in the nature of a reserve. It is probably not quite correct to call it "reserve" because it is, in fact, the manpower of the TO and that is called up in times of emergency, but it is to be contrasted with the permanent staff which are there all the time and, apparently, some witnesses do refer to it as "reserve".

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. MR. UZEIR BESIC, recalled.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Will there be any cross-examination of Mr. Besic? Mr. Tieger, are you finished -- you are. Mr. Wladimiroff, very good, OK.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, you have been interrogated in Germany in 1994, have you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I was interrogated in Germany.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: From your statement you have given to the German authorities, it appears that you have been asked, and I quote: "Mr. Besic, can you make statements about war crimes and acts by the accused Dusko Tadic that you witnessed first hand other than those about the two incidents you report in your notes?" Can you remember that, you have been asked this question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I gave statements about seeing Dule Tadic in the barracks and in the Omarska camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: That was, I take it, on the basis of your statement that you wrote yourself, your handwritten written statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I want to show the witness that statement for identification, please.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That will be Defence 15 -----

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I may not tender it so I just want it shown.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We still want to mark it for identification purposes so we will have a record of it. That will be what now, Mr. Bos? 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, could you just look at it and it has been typed out. Do you recognise that statement? It is not necessary that you read it all.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, generally, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I had not had an opportunity to look over the entire typed portion but, as Mr. Wladimiroff and the witness both indicated, it was a handwritten document which was made by the witness. I notice, for example, in this document quotation marks which I do not readily see in the handwritten document itself. I wonder if it would not be clearer and more useful to use the witness's original document?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Then I will show it to the witness, the handwritten document, though the copy is quite poor, I would say, but let us give it a try.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The handwritten is in his language, the typed version is in what language?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: In his own language.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: In his own language too. That will be marked Defence 16 for identification purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Is that your handwriting, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Why did you write that statement, Mr. Besic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I wrote the statement because this is the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did someone ask you to write that statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did this by myself and while I was writing this in Goettingen, I was there in a place for threatened peoples. I send it by fax there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did you send that by fax spontaneously or were you asked to do so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They asked for my statement because I told them that I saw Dule Tadic there and then I wrote in short what happened to me, how I came to the camp, where I saw him and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Who is "they"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those are people in Goettingen that work there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Is one of them called Mrs. Fadila Memisevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Fadila Memisevic yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Why did she approach you and ask you to write these notes? Was there a special reason to contact you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. On one occasion I was in Goettingen and we talked about suffering and I told my story and she told me to write something about that and I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So you wrote these notes on her request?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not at her request; at my request.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, have you featured in the Monika Gras film?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Were you questioned by Monika Gras or one of her associates? Were you interviewed for the purpose of that film?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mostly in Monika Gras' movie, that movie talked about the bodies up there where I was, the corpses, but one group went through Kozara and this is how it was found out that I was alive and this is how I got into the Monika Gras' movie.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: How many times were you interviewed by Monika Gras?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think twice before the film and then during the shooting of the movie.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Were those interviews broadcasted in that film on television?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Is it true then that this Fadila Memisevic saw you on that film and for that reason contacted you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think she saw me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So first you were interviewed by Monika Gras, then you were contacted by Mrs. Memisevic and then you presented to her your notes; is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I was in Goettingen and after that I wrote my notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, you also spoke to Professor Muenzel, do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did he interview you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was not exactly an interview; we just talked.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: For how long was that? How long did you talk?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not tell you exactly how long it lasted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Could it have been one hour, approximately?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Let us say it was one hour, maybe less, maybe more.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Were notes taken of that interview?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. He was taking some notes, but I do not know what was in those notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: This interview with Professor Muenzel, was that before you were interviewed by Monika Gras or was that after the Gras interview?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was after.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, you also gave interviews to French journalists, is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: From your German statement, it appears that you gave an interview to French journalists, so if I put this to you, do you remember it then again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I gave that interview in Goettingen.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did you speak to other people about your experiences and, more specifically, about Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Never since you arrived in Croatia after you left the area of Bosnia, you never spoke again about what happened to you except for what I just asked you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not understand the question well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did you speak with other persons about your events, what happened in Bosnia, more specifically about Dusko Tadic, with other people than the people I have mentioned before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not talk about Dusko Tadic, except with the people at Tribunal and when I gave the statement in Germany and in Goettingen.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Have you met other Bosnian Muslims who are living at a place where you live, in the country where you live, and did you discuss with those refugees what happened to you in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, where I live most of us there were detained in camps and everybody has his own story about the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I suppose you have exchanged your experiences with each other, have you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we were talking about specific events, how it was for us at the camp and, "Do you remember this or that?"

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: And "this and that" was not also related to Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, sometimes maybe there was something of that nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, in your statement today you told the court that you knew Dusko Tadic from Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: You did not know him well, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew him well enough. I was never in -- I never contacted him. I never was friends with him. We were not in the same company. He is older than me and he had his own company, but just from passing by. I mean, I think that every person that lived in Kozarac knew Dule Tadic because he was a famous person.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Why was he famous then, Mr. Besic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, he was famous for karate. He trained karate and he would come to the school, to the gym where we trained, and he would train there and other people trained with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: But in your statement today you said that when you were questioned, you were asked: "Did you sometimes watch Dule Tadic and your friends train?" Then you answered: "Well, sometimes, sometimes -- very seldom however"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So you hardly saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I saw Dule Tadic seldomly when he trained because I was not really interested in karate. As a child, sometimes as children, we would peak through the windows to see what they were doing there in the gym.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: You are older than Dusko Tadic, are you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that is not true that I am older.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: He is older than you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: How tall are you, Mr. Besic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I really do not know. I have not measured myself in a long time. I am not tall. I am short.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: If I come back to your contact with other refugees in the country where you live, and if I remind you of "this and that" also related to Dusko Tadic. Did you also discuss to whom Dusko Tadic is married and the composition of his family? Did other refugees make comments on that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I never made comments as to who is he married to. I never talked about his family with anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Do you remember when Dusko Tadic was arrested in Germany?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I remember somewhat.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: There was a lot of publicity, was there not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I watched it on television.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Later on, there were also broadcastings about the Tadic family, was that not the case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember what was said about his family. I watched his arrest and some details about how that happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I take it that you have seen the Monika Gras film, have you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: If I put to you, Mr. Besic, that Dusko Tadic does not know you, how come that you are claiming that you know him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I claim that I know Dusko Tadic, and I am firm about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Is it true that you have been shown a photograph of Dusko Tadic when you were interrogated by the German police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, let us move to the period of time before the conflict in 1992: you were a member of the TO, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was not a member of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, I want to show to this witness Exhibit D6, please. Mr. Bos, perhaps you could show the witness page A1-73? Mr. Besic, can you read what is typed down at the left top of this page?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Shall I read this?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Territorial Defence of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Headquarters in Kozarac".

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: What is typed -----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "TO Headquarters in Kozarac".

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you. What is on the right side typed "Besici" ---

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: -- that is a place where you were born?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: And where you lived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Could you read to the court the name which is typed beside No. 1?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It says "Besic Uzeir".

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: In handwriting it also says your name. Is that your handwriting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is right. That is my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So you signed on this list beside your name which is mentioned beside No. 1; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Could you place that paper on the right hand on the elmo? Perhaps Mr. Bos may do it? Thank you, Mr. Bos. Could you read what is written beside your name? I read something like "kusti" but you know better what it says?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is typed "Besic Uzeir" and then goes my signature, and then it says Russian -- Russian Dobosar.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It means the rifle produced, manufactured in Russia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Has that rifle been handed over to you while you signed on this list?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Do you know why this was written beside your name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This came on the list from TO in Kozarac, in case there was a need to mobilize all capable men. My house was the first in Besici and I was the first on the list, and it went, they went down through the list -- at least, that is what I think -- and I am not sure who was carrying those orders here; and we had to sign the mobilization order and in case something happened, there was an uprising or something, in that case I would be able to get this Russian rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Do you remember when you signed this mobilization list?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Immediately prior to attack on Kozarac -- perhaps a day or two before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: You just testified that, despite the attack was imminent, you did not get the gun or the pistol that is mentioned here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not get it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: On the right side it is written "Privatna"; is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: What does that mean, Mr. Besic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not sure. They probably added this later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Is it not true then that you had this rifle or gun at your home in private? You already had the weapon before you signed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that is not true. That is not true. I did not have a weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: In your evidence today you were questioned by the Prosecution and you were asked, I quote: "Had you heard about any talk about any individual attempting to organise some kind of defence?" and you responded to that question by saying, I quote again: "Yes, there were individuals who tried to do something, but all in all they did not succeed". Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember saying that there were individuals who were trying something, they were trying to create a defence of Kozarac, but that they did not succeed in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Were those individuals organised?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they were, I am not sure how they did that. I did not attend any meetings, so I do not know what they talked about and whether they were organised with police or TO. I really do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, if I may ask you now to look to your own statement and perhaps you would take the typed one or, if you prefer, you can look in your handwritten statement. If I may ask you to look at a passage which I would say -- no, it is not in your handwritten statement, excuse me. It is in your interview that you gave to the German authorities so I will read it to you. It is not in your own statement. You told in your German statement, and I will read it to you: "A former officer of the Yugoslav Army, a Muslim called Sead Cirkin, set up a small, lightly armed group consisting of members of the Territorial Defence forces and volunteers, and wanted to fight the Serbs". Do you remember that, saying to the German authorities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember. I do not remember saying something like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Do you know Sead Cirkin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not understand the question well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Do you know a person called Sead Cirkin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Who is he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sead Cirkin, I did not know him before the war. I think he was in the military. I heard about him. I saw him maybe a few times in Kozarac and that is all, and in the camp, Manjaca camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did you hear about him organising a small, lightly armed group consisting of members of the Territorial Defence and volunteers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard that he organised something, tried actually to organise a defence of Kozarac, but whether that was within the TO or within the police, I do not know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I ask you again, Mr. Besic, were you a member of this group of Sead Cirkin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was not a member of this group.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Do you know anyone who was a member of that group? Can you give me names?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not know any.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Has this group also been active under the command of Sead Cirkin in the area of Hambarine?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember. I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: When you were interviewed by the German authorities did you speak the truth to them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I speak the truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: But did you speak the truth then on that occasion in 1994 when you were interviewed by the German authorities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So how come that in your statement that you gave to the German authorities you tell them about Sead Cirkin organising or setting up a small lightly armed group consisting of members of the Territorial Defence forces and volunteers, is that true what you said on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did mention Sead Cirkin. I think I mentioned him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, in your evidence today you told the court that after you were apprehended and brought to the village of Besici that you were asked to step in a van that brought you to Prijedor. You do remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it is not true that I got on to the van in Besici.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Where was it then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was at Rajkovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: From there you went with this van to Prijedor, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With that, I was beaten up, tied with a wire. I was asked to identify a boy who was tied to a tree and then we were put on to a van and went to Prijedor, to the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: You testified today that you were able to see that you were heading towards Prijedor and you arrived at a JNA barrack?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I want to show a map to the witness for identification and I will tender it later on.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That will be Defence 17.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Perhaps you could put it on the elmo later on? Will you first show it to the witness and then later on -- Mr. Besic, can you tell us what this is, what is on this map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a map of sorts of Prijedor or I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Right. I will tender this map, your Honour. For your convenience, I made extra copies not only for the Prosecution but also for you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection, Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Not in principle. I would like to see the map first.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, there is no objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Defence 17 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, if you try to orientate yourself on this map, can you tell us where you entered Prijedor when you were in that van?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On this map?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: On that map, please. If you familiarise yourself with the map, would you please then put the map on the overhead screen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This map is not quite clear. I can explain where I came in, from which direction, but I cannot show it on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Are you able to locate on the map the military barracks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Do describe then how you came in Prijedor in this van and where approximately these barracks are?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I entered Prijedor after we came with this van and there were windows there so I could see something. I am familiar with the route, so when we entered Prijedor we turned right towards Bosanska Dubica.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: If you just stop there? You entered Prijedor from the north or was that from another direction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the direction of Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Right. You were driving on the main road then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, we drove down -- yes, the main road Banja Luka/Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Was that the new road or the old road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What do you mean old road, new road?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: That is the new road or the old road from Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The highway Banja Luka/Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Right, and entering the city of Prijedor did you pass by the factory of Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Probably we did, but I paid no attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: If you look at that map again, and if you look to the right side of that map, do you see a road starting on the right side?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot really, I am lost with this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Let us try again. You entered from the city of Prijedor on the outer route, where did you drive then? Where were you in Prijedor when you entered?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From Kozarac, I came out to the main road, Prijedor/Banja Luka. I moved towards Prijedor. I know I entered Prijedor and reached the barracks. When we arrived I knew I had arrived in the Prijedor barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Have you ever been before in those military barracks in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I have never been to the barracks in Prijedor. I have only passed by it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So you were familiar with the location of the military barracks? You have seen it before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was familiar with the barracks because I passed by it either riding a bus or a car on my way to Croatia through Bosanska Dubica. I often took this route.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Are those barracks in the centre or in the outskirts of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The barracks is not in the centre of the town; it is in the part, Puharska. I believe it is called Puharska.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Where is that in Prijedor, in north, south, east, west?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The barracks is on a route to Puharska, towards Bosanska Dubica.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: You do not know whether that is on the northern part, western part, southern part or eastern part?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I really do not have my sense of orientation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Is that a problem that is attached to a map or do you have a general problem with orientation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have problems with the locality.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I see. Arriving at that barracks you testified that was on June 3rd; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I arrived in the barracks on 3rd June.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: You also testified that you were brought into the barracks and then you were ordered to stop in a hallway where you were ordered to stand against the wall.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was ordered to enter the hallway and we stood against a wall in the hallway.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Facing the wall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Were you standing there alone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there was -- there were myself and those other two who had come with me from Rajkovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Where were they standing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was the first one since I had entered first and they were next to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: One on each side or both on one side?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was standing to the right and they both stood to the left next to the entrance.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Then you were beaten up by soldiers while you were standing in the hallway?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They beat us with batons as we stood there on our backs and shoulders.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So all three of you were beaten up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I was beaten and another one and that youngest boy, I am not quite sure if they beat him, I think, but I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Where were you beaten? Were you beaten in your face?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not the face. They beat us on our backs and shoulders.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: You then testified that you collapsed and fell on your knees; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not faint. I merely collapsed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: You were on your knees?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I fell down on my knees and was leaning against a wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Were you dizzy?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did the beating up hurt you much?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was pain but I was fighting, I wanted to live. I wanted to live.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did you have wounds? Were you wounded?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I take it that you were afraid, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we were. I was afraid but I was not wounded. My friend who came with me and the other one, he was wounded in the leg.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: While you were standing there beaten up by those soldiers, when they stopped where were the soldiers then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I fell down after those beatings, after those blows with a baton. I received a few kicks also and then I do not know where they went.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: You did not notice because you were beaten up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they were behind me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So while you were facing the wall you could not see what happened behind you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not see what was on my left.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: You could not see what was on your left. The other two persons were standing on your left, were they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did you see if they were beaten up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard cries of pain. One could hear the baton blows, one knows, and I knew later that he was beaten but each one was fighting for himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: In your statement you said that after this incident you saw Dusko Tadic coming out of a room while you were standing there in the hallway or lying on the ground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said I saw Dule Tadic while I was on my knees with my head against a wall and looking towards the right, and then Dule Tadic came out of a room and was moving towards the exit from that building.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Dusko Tadic came out of a room and you were moving towards the exit from that building at the same time; is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was not moving.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So you were just there on your knees?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, with my head against the wall looking towards right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Where was the room from which Dusko Tadic entered the hallway?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was to the right. I cannot say exactly which room it was, but he came out of one of the rooms.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: When he came out he passed you from your back side, did he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was walking towards us, and as he was coming he kicked me several times in the body and went out, I do not know where. I did not see him any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: When you say kicking you, that was with his feet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, with his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, would you mind to look in your handwritten statement or in the typed one, whatever you prefer? It is on the desk. Could you look in that, please? Then I ask you to look at the paragraph that starts with, "Then on June 3rd they took us, that is, me and the two old people, into Rajkovici village". Have you found that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I found it. Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: If you go down from there you will see much further on about I would say eleven lines -- I am not sure whether this is the same in your handwritten one -- "They tied the two of us with barbed wired and took us straight to the barracks in Prijedor". Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: " ... straight to the barracks in Prijedor", yes, true.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Can you keep your finger there so you will remember where you were in your statement? Once again, you were on your knees in the hallway, Dusko Tadic came out of a room, he passed by and he kicked you with his feet, right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He did not pass by me. It is not true he passed by me, but before he passed by me he kicked me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did he kick the other one -- no, the other two persons too or did he only kick you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember that he kicked them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Now let us go back to your finger. The next sentence begins: "When we got there they accused us" -- have you found that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we arrived in the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Then go to the next line and would you read that for me, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: " ... they accused the two of us of killing Serb children and raping".

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: The next line, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Then again they beat us both".

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: And the next line, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "They beat us and then they beat us in a hallway and from a room Dule Tadic in camouflage clothes came out and after that beating interrogation began". Should I go on?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Towards the end of this interrogation I was brought some paper to sign, and the paper said that I had participated in the armed rebellion against the Serbs in the Prijedor barracks. I did not know anyone except Dule Tadic".

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you. In my translation it says "he", and it refers to Dusko Tadic, "he hit us in the face too and beat us up".

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it is not true that he hit us in the face and beat us. They wrote it; I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Could you read that line again, what you have written there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they accused the two of us of killing.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: When you please start when Dule Tadic came out of the room, start there, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "From a room Dule Tadic in camouflage clothes came out and he then hit us. After that beating began, the interrogation. Towards the end of this interrogation" -----

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: "He hit us" and in your notes does it say "He hit us in the face"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no. It does not say so, and it is not true that he hit us in the face. I do claim that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Besic, after that you were brought to the Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not to the camp at Omarska, but to the camp in Keraterm. From the barracks I went to the camp at Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: You are right. I was mistaken indeed. After Keraterm you were brought to Omarska camp, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, after some time I was transferred from Keraterm to Omarska camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: You have told the court about the pista and you have shown where that pista is on the display in front of you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I showed where the pista was on the model.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Tell us again, when you were sitting on the pista, at what direction would you look?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was looking towards the structure where they conducted interrogations and the restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: When you were lying on the concrete you were looking at?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: While we were lying on the concrete, on the pista, we were facing the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: If you were sitting facing the restaurant, were you allowed to look around or were you ordered to look only in the direction of the restaurant?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were not ordered to look only somewhere. One could cast a glance here and there as we sat. It depended sometimes on the mood of the guards when we lie down on the pista.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I am not referring to lying down, but I am referring to sitting down. Were you allowed, when you were sitting down, to look to another direction, that is, not looking in the direction of the restaurant?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We mostly looked towards the canteen. One could look left and right. One could not really think about how everybody was, what everybody was looking at.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: When you were lying down were you allowed to look around?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It depended how one was lying and where his head was turned.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: You testified today that on some occasions you were ordered to lie down, and those occasions were beatings or when someone was carried out from interrogation, do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were ordered to lie down, especially when an incident would occur when they would beat up, severely someone, or when someone from the outside would come or if someone was carried dead from the interrogation and things like that, then we were ordered to lie down so as not to see something.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So you would not see what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So probably that it was so as not to see what was going on depending on the case of something.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: If there were beatings and you were ordered to lie down, I suppose that everyone followed strictly to that order in order not to get involved, is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not quite understand the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: If there were beatings on the pista and you were ordered to lie down, I take it that no one was looking around, not taking the risk that you could get involved in those beatings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. When there were beatings, yes, we were in the prone position, we were lying down in the prone position on the stomach, and one could perhaps cast a look sideways depending on the blows. When we were lying down on the pista the head was not down, I mean not nose to the ground; it would be turned sideways to one side or the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Have you heard about occasions when people were punished because they were looking around while they were ordered to lie down facing the concrete?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember such cases. I think there were such cases but I do not remember any one of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: You told us today that when you were on the pista your attention was drawn because you heard sounds coming from the direction of the restaurant building; is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Behind the canteen.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Right. What was your association at that moment - beatings? Did you think about beatings? Did you connect that sound with beatings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I associated it with beating. When I heard something like that we knew that somebody was being hit, that they were dealing blows, and then one could hear cries of pain or screams "oh" "aargh" and they would be running towards the pista. So that was how I cast a look towards them to the direction from which they were coming.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: You were then ordered to lie down facing the concrete?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before that I saw that group when they ran out. It all happened very fast, and it was then that I saw Tadic and some other soldiers and then it came "Lie down".

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: While they were running in the direction of the pista you saw Dusko Tadic and you were ordered lie down; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I saw -- it all happened very fast, you know, they were coming from behind the canteen and just as they turned the corner the order came to lie down.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So you laid down, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, as the orders came.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Facing the ground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Then the group ran to the side next to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That group of inmates, there was room next to me on the right side because I was towards the end and I think they were also given the order to lie down on the pista also in the prone.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Were guards standing in the vicinity of you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember if there were any guards next to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Would you dare to take the risk that you would get involved in these beatings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know what you mean by "risk"?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Would you do anything that might cause the risk that you would be involved in those beatings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Would you just stand up to see what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I would not stand up, for sure not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Would you sit down and see what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I would not sit down. If I stood up or sat up I think that would be a great risk.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Would you raise your head to look around?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would raise my head a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: You took the risk by raising your head a little bit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, at that moment I was not really thinking about the risk.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: While the others were beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was interested, I wanted to confirm once again who was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, I suggest that you did not look because you were afraid to get involved and you have been told this story?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not think that I gave a false story. I am telling you exactly what happened.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Wladimiroff, are you moving into an another area?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I have two things to ask and then I am finished. Mr. Besic, do you know Mr. Danicic, a person called Mr. Danicic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Before you entered this courtroom today to give your statement, have you been in this courtroom before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Was I in this courtroom?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes, before you gave your statement today were you shown the courtroom before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was shown to me, the courtroom was shown to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: And was it told to you where all persons would sit, the Judges the Defence, the Prosecution, the Defendant?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was shown where the Judges would sit, the Defence, but they did not show me where the accused was going to sit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Were you told where the Prosecution would be sitting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Do you mean Tadic's Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Prosecution? Yes, it was shown to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Where would you expect Tadic to sit -- at the side of the Defence or at the side of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not expect, I did not know where he would sit. I did not know where Tadic would sit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you. No further questions, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: If we can finish with this witness, let us see if we can do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let me suggest something quickly, if I may, before I ask the witness questions and perhaps I can address this to the Defence through the Court. I want to make sure there is no suggestion that there was any inaccuracy in the witness's re-reading of his statement as it was interpreted to this court, otherwise I would like someone independent to re-read it. I do not want to have that issue revisited. When he re-read the portions that Mr. Wladimiroff insisted he had another interpretation on, a bad interpretation as it happens.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Wladimiroff, it seems that your English translation as I heard you read it and as the witness then read his written statement in his language, there was a difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: So, Mr. Tieger wants to ask you to agree that the witness read his statement correctly and that your translation just was different.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes. The translation that has been provided to me by the Tribunal appears to be the translation of the typed version of the statements. Apparently there is a difference between the typed version and the handwritten version, but at this stage I would say I will check it myself and see whether there is any difference on that specific line. I take it that there is a difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The typed version is not different.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Is not different? If you check that then I take it that the translation was not accurate, but I will check that too.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That can, of course, be checked later. I just wanted to satisfy everyone that the reading was correct and apparently Mr. Wladimiroff agrees.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I suppose that the reading was correct because I read with the witness, though with the typed version, but I will check with the written version too. So there is a difference apparently.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, are you satisfied or do you want to handle it differently? We do not need to rush through this. We can call the witness back tomorrow, however you want to handle it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, at this point I do not know how else to resolve it. I think a look at the written version makes it clear that the words are exactly the same as in the typed version, but I cannot force that on Mr. Wladimiroff if he is concerned about potential differences.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, he read what he read. I agree he did not read something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: OK, fine. He read his handwritten version.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Fine. I will check that at least from the typed one. That is the same, but the real issue here is what about the quality the translation here? I am not able to make any comments on that at this stage.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The written statement in Serbo-Croat is the same as the typed statement in Serbo-Croat. The difference is in the English translation. OK. Does that satisfy you?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The written and the typed Serbo-Croatian are the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And the witness read verbatim from his handwritten statement.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: He read what was written on the Serbo-Croatian statement, the handwritten one, is that correct? OK. Very good.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Just a few questions, Mr. Besic. Mr. Wladimiroff asked you some questions about Sead Cirkin. The fact is, Mr. Besic, that you expressly mentioned Sead Cirkin to the Germans, is that right, at least according to the statement that was written down by the Germans?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I think I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you also tell the German authorities that the Muslims in Kozarac wanted a peaceful solution to the conflict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you also say that whatever Sead Cirkin was trying to do you could not say how big the group was, for example?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not estimate that, but I think that it was not a large number.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In fact, when the war, when the attack on Kozarac took place you saw no evidence of any organised defence that had been set up in advance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not see anything. When the attack on Kozarac started it was not possible to defend Kozarac and I think that there was not any kind of defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In any event, you were not trying to hide Sead Cirkin from the German authorities, and you mentioned him explicitly to them and it was written in the German statement, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Wladimiroff also asked you if the German authorities showed you a photograph of Dule Tadic. Do you recall that question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Did they show me a picture of Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: He asked you that question, is that right, and you told him you had seen a photograph of Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was a picture I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: He did not ask you about any other photographs you were shown. Were you shown a series of photographs of people and asked to see if you recognised Dule Tadic among those photographs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No, there were several pictures, and I do not know exactly how many there were and I was told to recognise the people that I knew, to show the people that I knew. Among those pictures there was also a picture of Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you know whether or not there were at least 14 pictures, since his is labelled No. 14 in the statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember what number it was labelled under.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, just out of curiosity, do you know what kind of rifle a Ruski Dobosar is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I know that. I have seen it in the army. Members of the TO had that. The TO in Kozarac had that rifle, Ruski Dobosar. It is a short rifle that had one drum of munition, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How old is that rifle? Is it older than an M48, for example?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it is older.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, can I ask you to look once again at Defence Exhibit, the page of Defence Exhibit 6 which you were shown? Looking at that list of 38 people who were alive in Besici just a few days before the attack, can you tell us the names of people on that list who are dead or have never been seen again by their friends or families since the attack on Kozarac or in their placement and camps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can. I would ask not to mention the name of the people. I would just mention the number because I know there are still parents looking for their children and I cannot say about some. I can know about some that I am sure are dead, but some others are not confirmed and there are hopes that they will reappear.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That is an excellent suggestion, sir. I am sure no one has any objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, I have no objection to mentioning a number as such, but I have some problem with this witness answering the question because how could he know?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Well, that goes to the weight and you will be able to cross-examine, so I will overrule it on that basis. It is really beyond redirect, that is for sure. So if you have that objection I will sustain it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK, it is sustained.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Go ahead, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Or it is beyond cross, actually.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just the number?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would have to take a look at this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I said it is beyond cross-examination. It was offered only for the purpose of showing that the witness had signed, number one, and whatever was adjacent to his name. So really he did not go into it on cross-examination. It is beyond cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Very well, your Honour. Mr. Besic, I withdraw that question. You do not need to answer it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Wladimiroff?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No further questions, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I just have one question. What were the dates you were in Omarska camp, Mr. Besic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The dates, I do not remember exactly what date it was when I came to Omarska, but when Omarska was closed I remained there for another 20 days after everyone else, after everybody else. I was registered by the Red Cross at Omarska camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you recall the date when you testified that you saw Mr. Tadic on the pista?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Do I remember the date?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not remember the exact date.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, do you have additional questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can I have just one moment, your Honour?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, you arrived in Omarska at the beginning of June, approximately June 3rd, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To Omarska?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Excuse me, to Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Then you were in Keraterm approximately two weeks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Approximately, maybe less, maybe more. I do not remember exactly any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you remember how long you were in room 15 until you were interrogated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Let us say 20 days, 25 days, I am not sure exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After the interrogation you were taken to the pista?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, after interrogation I went to pista.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Wladimiroff, do you have additional questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Just one, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, just to assist the court, can you tell us how do you know that you arrived in Keraterm on June 3rd?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know it was June 3rd because it was 31st May when the Serb Army arrested us, took us prisoners. I know it was June 3rd, I remember that well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: But it needs an additional question, your Honour. How do you know you were arrested on May 31st?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know it was May 31st. I think it was a Sunday.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Is there any specific reason why you have that date in mind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was, yes, a reason for me to know this. When the people from my group were killed by Kozarac Kamen. I remember that relatively well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No further questions, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Nothing further, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection to Mr. Besic being permanently excused?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: No objection. Mr. Besic, you are permanently excused. You may leave. Thank you for coming. We will stand adjourned until tomorrow at 10 a.m.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: (The court adjourned until the following day). 24 25

procedural_notes.text: (The court adjourned for a short time)
